build.summary: Filings draws the current recently-played cover (centre-cropped and sampled at 128²) as 3,200 to 9,000 round-capped iron filings. They are rendered in raw WebGL2 as one instanced draw, with a capsule SDF per filing and a grain paper pass, and fall back to Canvas2D at half the count if WebGL2 isn't available. Tone sets each filing's length and width. At rest, each filing lies along the cover's edge-tangent flow, taken from a blurred structure tensor, so the picture reads as a flow-line engraving rather than a horizontal hatch. Each flat pill magnet is a DOM button modelled as two opposite 2D poles. A preallocated CPU sim runs damped doubled-angle dynamics (K 260, c from the Wobble slider, plus a little stiction so filings come to rest), creep toward the poles, and chaining along field lines. The chaining comes from the poles' stream function, which nudges filings into streaks. Only N×3 floats are uploaded per frame, the loop sleeps when everything settles, offscreen or hidden. Every interaction in the brief is in: drag with pointer capture, tap or F to flip (a 380ms/0.18 spring, so the field sweeps round), wheel, R or a two-finger twist to rotate, double-click or double-tap to add (up to 3, popping in at 0.84→1.02→1 with blur), drag off the edge to remove, shake by wiggling or S, and arrow keys to move. Six cover chips morph the picture filing by filing, staggered outward from the nearest magnet. The caption changes with MorphText and the panel numbers roll with SlotNumber. The panel has three looks (Iron, Cover colour, Blueprint), five sliders, and Shake, Save PNG and Reset.
build.wowMoment: The filings bloom outward from the magnet with an easeOutBack stagger and swing from random angles into a fan of field lines. About 2.6s later, if nobody has touched it, the magnet flips once on its spring and the whole field sweeps round, so every filing swings through in a visible ripple. Put two magnets nose to nose and the filings between them part. Tap one to flip it and a bridge of streaked lines snaps between the poles. Drag the magnets away and the cover combs itself back into its engraving.
build.knownIssues: Not seen in a browser (per the rules). It was checked only by the three checks passing, eslint coming back clean, and a Node run of the simulation. That run, at 8,100 filings, showed 0.7ms per step, no NaNs, creep capped at 6px, 99% of the filings near the magnet aligned to the field, and about 32% of the plate dominated by the magnet at the default field strength. A small number of filings in weak-field spots can drift slowly for a long time, so after 3.5s without input the loop treats anything under 0.35 rad/s as settled and goes idle, and that leftover drift freezes in place. Chaining uses the poles' stream function (filings move sideways into field-line lanes, capped at 0.42 of the spacing) instead of a neighbour grid hash. On phones and other touch screens both creep and chaining are off, as the brief asks. On short viewports (the 76vh taste iframe) the controls panel in the side column runs past the fold, but the plate stays top-aligned and fully visible. The one-time automatic flip at 2.6s is my addition, not in the brief. Before the cover image loads, the plate shows warm paper even in the Blueprint look.

critique.firstFrame: A warm #f5f2ea plate with grain and a faint edge vignette. The flat half-ink pill magnet pops in at lower right (scale 0.84 to 1 with blur) while the plate is still empty, because the scene mounts before the cover has loaded and been sampled. Once the 128 by 128 sample lands (one network fetch plus about 10ms of work), the canvas fades in over 900ms. At the same time about 9,000 filings grow outward from the magnet with easeOutBack, starting at random angles and swinging into place: a fan of field lines around the magnet and, everywhere else, an engraving that follows the cover's edges (the structure-tensor rest field). It reads as the cover drawn in filings, not as Ink-style horizontal hatching. On any desktop plate wider than about 735px, the bottom-right edge row is missing 25 filings, a visible notch (see the layout bug). If nothing has been touched by 2.6s, the magnet flips itself on its spring and a swing ripples outward. The right column holds the title, one line of instructions, a MorphText caption, six staggered cover chips and a quiet controls card. It is a strong, physical first frame, but it shows one magnet. The brief's wow (two magnets nose to nose, flip one, the field becomes a bridge) only happens if the visitor reads the instructions, double-clicks the paper and positions a second magnet themselves.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate filings: PASS. 2. compile-check filings: PASS (9 modules). 3. glsl-check src/app/lab/filings: all 4 shader sources ok (filingsShader.js:1, :53, :73, :86). There are no interpolations, so the check is meaningful. Code review: the WebGL2 calls are correct (5-arg bufferSubData lengths are element counts, the divisor-0 corner attribute is present, VAOs are captured properly). Uniforms are all set each draw. Blending is premultiplied and consistent. Context loss and restore are handled. The Canvas2D fallback runs at N/2. There is no per-frame React state, no getImageData per frame, rect is cached during drags, and the loop runs on demand with idle detection and pauses for hidden tabs and offscreen. dispose removes every listener, observer, timer and the GL context. Nothing touches window during SSR. The physics is correct: doubled-angle torque, a monopole-pair field normalised so B_ref does not depend on size, and a stream-function lane offset with the right sign whose atan2 branch cut lands on an integer number of lanes. The piece uses raw WebGL2 instead of the R3F the brief asked for, which is acceptable and lighter.

issues.problem: layout() uses columns = round(sqrt(count)) and total = min(MAX_FILINGS, columns²). At the desktop default (count capped at 9000), columns = 95, so 9025 is clamped to 9000. The last row holds only 70 of its 95 cells, which leaves a bare notch 25 filings wide along the bottom-right edge of the plate in the first frame on every plate wider than about 735px.
issues.fix: Use columns = Math.floor(Math.sqrt(Math.min(count, MAX_FILINGS))) and total = columns * columns, so the grid is always full and square. Alternatively, keep the count and spread the remainder across rows: columns = ceil(sqrt(count)), rows = ceil(count / columns), with spacing per axis.

issues.problem: Two-finger twist ends in an unwanted flip. startTwist never marks the anchor finger's entry as moved, and onPointerMove only sets moved when !twist. If the anchor finger held still while twisting (the normal way to twist) and the twisting finger lifts first, the anchor's later pointerup reaches `completed && !entry.moved` (line 634) and flips the magnet 180°, undoing the gesture.
issues.fix: In startTwist, look up the anchor entry and set it moved: `const anchorEntry = pointers.get(anchorId); if (anchorEntry) anchorEntry.moved = true;`. The same path covers the `magnet && magnet.held` second-finger branch.

issues.problem: The magnet's entry animation `filings-magnet-in 440ms ... both` keeps `opacity: 1`, `transform: scale(1)` and `filter: blur(0)` from its last keyframe forever. Animation values outrank normal author declarations, so the `[data-removing]` fade to opacity 0 and the `[data-leaving]` opacity 0.45 never apply. Dragging a magnet off the edge shrinks it to 0.88 at full ink, then it disappears abruptly after 260ms, which is the opposite of the brief's fade. The chips have the same problem: `filings-chip-in ... both` pins filter: blur(0), so the `:disabled` grayscale on a failed cover never shows.
issues.fix: Use `animation-fill-mode: backwards` for filings-magnet-in and filings-chip-in, since only the pre-start state needs holding. Or move the entry animation onto the outer `.filings-magnet` wrapper's child and drop opacity and filter from the final keyframe. Then the data-leaving and data-removing transitions, and the chip grayscale, take effect.

issues.problem: The Density slider does nothing on desktop over most of its range. With PLATE_AREA_PER_FILING = 60, an 880px plate gives raw = 12,906 × density/100, which is above the 9,000 cap for any density ≥ 70%, so 70–140% all give 9,000. Every step that does change the count runs relayout(), which re-randomises every angle and regrows the whole plate. Dragging the slider makes the picture strobe.
issues.fix: Map density against the cap: count = clamp(MAX × density/140, MIN, ceiling), with the area rule only lowering the ceiling on small plates. Debounce relayout until the slider's pointerup, or relayout with mode 'morph' that keeps the existing theta for surviving indices.

issues.problem: Shake detection counts sign reversals on x and y together, at 3px per event. A fast circular stir, the most natural thing to do with a magnet over filings, produces about 4 reversals in under 400ms and fires a whole-plate ±18 rad/s scramble every 600ms. That wipes out the combing the visitor was making.
issues.fix: Track reversals only on the dominant axis of motion, and require each half-stroke to travel at least 24px (keep an extremum and count a reversal only when the pointer returns 24px past it). Then only a deliberate back-and-forth shake triggers it.

issues.problem: The canvas fades from opacity 0 over 900ms at the same moment the filings start their easeOutBack grow. The filings nearest the magnet, which pop first, are half hidden by the fade, so the intro's overshoot reads as a soft dissolve. The host is already the same paper colour, so the fade only hides the paper grain.
issues.fix: Drop the canvas opacity fade, or cut it to 200ms. Let the per-filing scale-up be the reveal, since the paper-coloured host already matches the first paper draw.

issues.problem: Clicking a chip whose sample is still waiting on requestIdleCallback (up to 1.2s) changes the caption and active ring straight away, but the plate keeps the previous cover until the sample arrives. Caption and picture disagree. Also, if every remote cover fails CORS sampling, all chips are disabled and the plate stays a blank sheet with a magnet forever. There is no client fallback to the /flyout cards.
issues.fix: Sample on demand when a chip is clicked (call sampleCover synchronously if the image has decoded) and only move shownIndex once the sample exists. If every chip is FAILED, swap chips to the local /flyout FALLBACK covers, which are same-origin and always sample.

issues.problem: Creep is forced to 0 on compact or coarse-pointer devices, but the Creep slider still shows in the mobile drawer and does nothing. The closed mobile drawer is moved off-screen with translate only, so its sliders and buttons stay in the tab order and in the accessibility tree.
issues.fix: Hide the Creep control when compact (pass compact into FilingsControls). Put `inert` on .filings-panel-slot while data-panel is closed below 900px.

issues.problem: Nothing on the plate signals that empty paper takes a double-click: the cursor is the default arrow and there is no hover response off the magnet. The 2.6s auto-flip only fires if `touched` is false, but chip and panel clicks don't set touched, so it can flip while the visitor is busy in the panel.
issues.fix: Give the plate `cursor: crosshair` (or copy) when fewer than 3 magnets exist, and show a faint ghost pill under the pointer on fine-pointer hover that pops into the real magnet on double-click. Set touched from any chip or panel interaction.

critique.wowGap: Make the 2-magnet bridge the opening act instead of something the visitor has to find. After the filings settle (about 1.8s), auto-add a second magnet nose to nose with the first, about 0.22 of the plate apart along its axis and oriented so like poles face each other. It pops in with the existing 440ms entrance, and the filings between them visibly part into the repulsion gap. At about 3.4s, flip it on the 380ms/0.18 spring so the field swings into a bridge of lines joining the poles, rippling outward through the cover. Cancel the whole sequence on the first pointer or key. With that, the first five seconds show the brief's wow moment.

build.summary: Strum turns the site's type scale into a harp. Each string is one of Herb's recent song titles, set at 12 × r^n px with the tracking law worked out in JS and a live mono readout (size · tracking) that rolls after each size settles. Everything is drawn on one canvas by an imperative class (StrumHarp.js). Every glyph is placed by its measured advances, which are interpolated across weights 400, 600 and 900. That means the swell up to +260 weight changes the spacing instead of making glyphs collide. Each string is six damped harmonics, and the same b_n coefficients drive both the picture and the WebAudio voice (strumVoice.js): six sine partials, a 3 ms bandpassed noise pick, a pitch glide on hard plucks, a 16-voice cap with stealing, and a compressor on the output. You strum by crossing baselines: coalesced pointer segments are tested against each line, with a speed gate when hovering with a mouse. You can also press a line to bend it with a rounded apex and let go to twang it; pull past about 1.6× the reach and it slips off your finger and keeps strumming the lines below. Keys 1–0 pluck single lines and Space (Shift+Space) strums the whole scale. The ten-detent ratio slider re-springs every size with a 30 ms stagger (stiffness 170, damping 22), pops lines in and out, morphs the interval name, rolls the ratio, and maps each string to the nearest chord tone, so a sweep always lands on a chord.
build.wowMoment: Pull the biggest title down like a bowstring. The string turns accent blue and bends with a rounded apex under your finger. The letters ride the curve, tilt along its slope and get heavier near the apex, and they can dip below the stage onto the controls because the canvas extends past it. When you let go it twangs: the line blurs into the two soft curves of a vibrating string while the glyphs wobble on the same harmonics you hear. Then switch to the perfect fifth and the waterfall re-springs line by line into a new chord.
build.knownIssues: Not checked in a browser, as instructed. The logic was smoke-tested in Node with a mocked DOM and canvas: layout, bend, release, hover strum, ratio change, Space strum, and the loop going idle all ran with no NaN transforms. Not yet confirmed on real devices: (1) that Safari and Chrome draw canvas text at in-between variable weights such as 720 or 860; if one doesn't, the swell falls back to the nearest weight it has. (2) The pop-in blur uses an offscreen-shadow trick, so it works without ctx.filter, but it hasn't been looked at. (3) Before the first click or keypress, hover strums are silent because browsers block audio until then; the hint says "Click once for sound" until it unlocks, then morphs to the playing hint. (4) In the 76vh taste iframe at 1280 wide about 9 lines fit and the largest is about 72px; the roughly 110px bottom line only shows on a tall viewport. (5) touch-action: none on the stage means a phone page can only be scrolled from the header or footer, as the brief asks. (6) While a line is springing to a new size, its text is already truncated for the target size, so an ellipsis can show slightly early. page.js now falls back to the Please Please Me tracklist instead of "Card NN" titles, and the isProdView guard is unchanged.

critique.firstFrame: Before hydration: the header ("Strum" plus a secondary hint), a mute pill, and the footer ("Major third 1.250" with the detent slider) bracket a large empty light stage. Nothing is server-rendered on the canvas. Within one frame of mount, the waterfall of hairline strings and Geist titles pops in top to bottom: 0.84 to 1.02 to 1 with a 6px blur, staggered 45ms. On a roughly 900px desktop that is 11 lines from 12px to 112px, the longest titles on the small strings and short words like "Anna" and "Boys" huge at the bottom. Mono readouts such as "111.8 · −4.29" sit right-aligned on each string. From 380ms a silent pick ripples down the strings 70ms apart, each string blooming into a soft accent envelope while the glyphs ride the wave, and everything settles by about 3s. It is a strong, legible, quiet-Swiss first frame. The only weakness is the blank stage before JS runs.
critique.checks: 1. node scripts/lab-gate.mjs strum: PASS (lint, comments, type system, tokens). 2. compile-check.mjs strum: PASS (6 modules). 3. glsl-check.mjs src/app/lab/strum: "no shaders found". The piece is Canvas2D and WebAudio only, so this check does not apply. All three pass.

issues.problem: handlePointerDown overwrites this.gesture with no check. If one finger is bending a line and a second finger touches (natural on a harp), the first gesture is lost. That line keeps held=true forever: it stays bent in accent, crossLines skips it, and stepLines returns busy every frame, so rAF never idles. The first finger's pointerup then fails the gesture.id check and returns early.
issues.fix: Keep gestures in a Map keyed by pointerId: this.gestures.set(event.pointerId, {...}), look up by event.pointerId in move and up, and delete on up or cancel. Two fingers can then strum and bend independently. At minimum, if a gesture already exists, call this.release(previous.line, time) before replacing it. Also handle lostpointercapture like pointercancel.

issues.problem: Weight is driven by the instantaneous |y|, which passes through zero twice per cycle. At visualHz up to 12, the weight flickers between rest and +260 at up to 24Hz. On the small 12–24px lines a strike exceeds the 0.25·band reach, so they strobe between 460 and 720 rather than swelling and relaxing. It reads as a flashing glitch rather than a string glowing bold.
issues.fix: Drive the swell from the per-glyph envelope already computed in displacementAt (this.sampleEnvelope), which decays smoothly: weight = rest + SWELL * min(1, sampleEnvelope / reach). Keep |y| only while line.held, so the bend still thickens under the finger.

issues.problem: The pen accumulates the swollen advance (advanceAt at the live weight), so the whole word widens and narrows with the swell. The right end of a vibrating title shimmers horizontally, and swollen display lines overrun textRight into the readout gutter. The brief pins glyphs at rest advances so weight swells without reflow.
issues.fix: Advance the pen with restAdvance only. Draw each glyph centred on its rest centre (centreX = TEXT_X + (pen + restAdvance/2 - TEXT_X)*scale, fillText at -advance/2) so the swell grows symmetrically. Cap SWELL per size, e.g. SWELL * clamp(48/size, 0.45, 1), so 110px glyphs at 860 never touch.

issues.problem: Every tick clears and redraws every line. During a full strum each glyph has its own weight (50 steps of 10) and a unique rotation. That means up to about 250 context.font sets, which thrash Chrome's roughly 50-entry canvas font cache across 11 sizes, plus about 250 rotated large-glyph rasterisations per frame at DPR 2. During the intro, every glyph is also drawn with shadowBlur (lines 948–953) for about 440ms. A mid-range phone will drop frames in exactly the first 1.5 seconds Herb judges.
issues.fix: Quantise weight to 20-unit steps (13 levels), and skip rotation (slope=0) for lines under 20px, where it is invisible. Cache each resting line into its own offscreen canvas at rest weight, and blit it for lines whose energy is 0 and that are not held, so only ringing lines are re-rasterised. Do the pop-in blur once per line with drawImage(lineCanvas) under ctx.filter = `blur(${b}px)` instead of per-glyph shadows.

issues.problem: visualHz reaches 12, so harmonics 3 to 6 run at 36–72Hz, above the 30Hz Nyquist of a 60fps display. They alias into backwards or wrong-speed jitter. With a 12Hz fundamental, one cycle spans about 5 frames, so the small strings shake rather than wobble.
issues.fix: Clamp visualHz to about 2–7Hz (frequency/80). In the rotation loop, zero any harmonic whose n·visualHz exceeds 25Hz, or let it decay with GAMMA·n·4 so it never aliases.

issues.problem: The first interaction is silent. unlock() calls resume() asynchronously, so the keydown that unlocks (keys 1–0 or Space) checks this.ready while the state is still 'suspended' and returns. On iOS a tap pluck fires on pointerup, before the touchend unlock, so the first tap is mute. The first gesture is the one that has to land.
issues.fix: In pluck(), if this.context exists but state !== 'running', push the pluck args to a pending list. In unlock(), use this.context.resume().then(() => flush pending plucks whose timestamp is under 250ms old). Also add a 'statechange' listener that flushes the list.

issues.problem: resize() sets canvas.width and height, which clears the canvas immediately, but the redraw waits for the next rAF. ResizeObserver callbacks run after rAF in the same frame, so every resize step paints one blank frame and the waterfall flickers while the window is dragged.
issues.fix: Call this.positionLines(); this.draw(); synchronously at the end of resize(), after layout(), then kick().

issues.problem: On a ratio change, truncate() runs at the target size while the line is still at its old size. When lines shrink (fifth to third), a line shows its longer target glyph count at the larger size for about 0.5s and runs past textRight into the readout.
issues.fix: In drawGlyphs, stop drawing once pen exceeds this.textRight - TEXT_X and draw the ellipsis there. Alternatively, re-run truncate(line, line.size) when the spring settles and use min(count at size, count at target) while moving.

issues.problem: loadCovers dedupes recent tracks by album image and needs 6 or more unique images, a leftover from a covers piece. Strum only needs titles. Several top tracks from one album collapse to one, and the page can fall back to the Please Please Me list even when Herb has real titles.
issues.fix: Dedupe by lowercased cleaned title, don't require an image, and lower the threshold to 4 titles. Pass { title } objects only.

issues.problem: HINT_LOCKED says 'Click once for sound' on phones as well, where the gesture is a tap.
issues.fix: Choose the verb with matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)') through useSyncExternalStore: 'Tap once for sound, then swipe across the lines'.

issues.problem: The focusable stage div has an aria-label but no role, so screen readers ignore the label. Its keyboard instructions are never announced.
issues.fix: Add role="application" (or role="group") with aria-roledescription="harp", and keep the aria-label.

issues.problem: Before hydration the stage is an empty block, around 600px tall on desktop, between the header and the footer. Pop-in hides most of this, but on a slow connection the first paint is a blank page.
issues.fix: Server-render a static, aria-hidden waterfall of the titles at the default ratio (DOM spans with law tracking from strumScale), and fade it out on the harp's first draw. Alternatively, reserve the space with hairline strings in CSS so the frame is never empty.

critique.wowGap: Make the slider audible. The brief's whole thesis is "the ratio is the chord you hear," but changing the interval is silent. Today you change it, then have to go back and sweep the strings to hear what you picked. When the ratio's size springs settle (debounce about 220ms after the last detent change, and only once audio is unlocked), have the harp run a soft strum(1) at about 0.45 strength with a 40ms gap. Dragging the slider from Major third to Perfect fifth then resizes the waterfall and rings the new chord down it the moment the lines land. Each detent also plays the root plus that interval's tone as a tiny two-note pluck (amplitude 0.2). The slider becomes a tuning peg and the core idea is understood without explanation.

changes: StrumHarp.js: gestures are now kept in a Map keyed by pointerId, so two fingers can bend and strum on their own. lostpointercapture is handled like pointercancel, and a line that pops out hands its gesture over to strumming, so no line can stay held forever.

StrumHarp.js: weight swell comes from the smoothly decaying per-glyph envelope (sampleEnvelope). The |y| drive is used only while a line is held, so there is no more 24Hz strobing between 460 and 720.

StrumHarp.js: the pen moves by rest advances only and each glyph is drawn centred on its rest centre. The swell is capped per size (SWELL * clamp(48/size, 0.45, 1)), so words no longer shimmer horizontally or run into the readout gutter.

StrumHarp.js perf: weights are rounded to 20-unit steps (26 levels) and each line's font strings are prebuilt per size. Ringing lines are drawn in two passes grouped by weight, so the font is set once per level instead of once per glyph. Lines under 20px and slopes under 0.004 skip rotation.

StrumHarp.js perf: each resting line is cached in its own offscreen canvas at rest weight and copied in with one drawImage. Only ringing, held, flashing or resizing lines are drawn glyph by glyph. The pop-in blur is one ctx.filter blur per line instead of shadowBlur on every glyph, and the cache canvases are freed on dispose.
StrumHarp.js: wobble speed now maps pitch on a log scale to 2–7Hz. Any harmonic above 25Hz is damped away in about 30ms, so the small strings wobble instead of aliasing into jitter.
StrumHarp.js: resize() redraws straight away after layout, so dragging the window no longer flashes blank frames. Fixed a double-rAF: kick() called inside tick used to schedule a second frame.

StrumHarp.js: truncation is computed without allocating and uses the smaller of the fits at the current size and at the target size. It is reapplied every spring step, so shrinking lines never overrun the readout.

StrumHarp.js wowGap: setTuning takes a chord flag that schedules a soft strum (strength 0.45, 40ms gap). It fires 220ms after the last detent change once every line has landed (springs within 0.5px, pop-ins visible), and is dropped after 2.4s.

strumVoice.js: a pluck that arrives while the context is not running yet is queued, then flushed on resume().then and on statechange. A note is dropped once it is more than 250ms past its intended time, and the queue is cleared while the page is hidden. The first key, tap or slider touch is now audible.

strumVoice.js wowGap: chime(ratio) plays C4 and then C4 × ratio 45ms later at amplitude 0.2, panned left and right. It fires on every detent change through selectInterval, so the slider works as a tuning peg.

StrumExperience.jsx: the waterfall is server-rendered as an aria-hidden placeholder: real titles at the default ratio, law tracking from strumScale, token weights, hairlines with round end pins. A column-wrap flex hides rows that don't fit with the same rule the canvas uses. Each row blurs out with the canvas's 45ms stagger when the harp first draws (data-live).

StrumExperience.jsx: the hint picks Tap/swipe or Click/sweep through a (pointer: coarse) useSyncExternalStore. The stage has role=application and aria-roledescription=harp. The tuning effect passes voice.unlocked as the chord flag.
strumScale.js: exports bandFor, baselineDrop, DISPLAY_FROM and POP_IN_STAGGER_MS, so the canvas and the server-rendered placeholder share the same geometry.

page.js: titles are deduped by cleaned, lowercased title with no image needed. The threshold is 4 titles, it passes { title } objects only, the cache key is renamed to strum-titles, and the isProdView guard is kept.

strum.css: styles for the placeholder (string, pins, exact baseline via a flex spacer, narrow-gutter container query, staggered blur-out, reduced-motion overrides). Vertical values stay on the 4px grid and weights come from tokens.
experiment.json: description rewritten in two sentences around the audible ratio, tags changed to Audio, Type, Canvas, intent kept, building false, status still candidate.
polish.remaining: All three checks pass: lab-gate prints PASS, compile-check prints PASS (6 modules), and glsl-check found no shaders. Nothing was run in a browser, as required; everything else was checked by reading the code. Things to check in the browser: (1) whether ctx.filter blur ignores the canvas transform. I assumed it does and pass blur × dpr, the same as the old shadowBlur. If it doesn't, the pop-in blur is twice as strong at DPR 2. (2) Small rows of the server-rendered placeholder use --font-weight-meta (440), because there is no 460 token, while the canvas uses 460. They only cross-fade for about 240ms. (4) Ellipsis in the placeholder needs text-overflow to work with overflow-x: clip; where it doesn't, the line is hard-clipped instead.

The piece is Canvas2D and WebAudio, so this check does not apply. Round-1 fixes, verified in the code. (a) Multi-touch: gestures now live in a Map keyed by pointerId (line 162). issues.problem: The entrance plays twice. The SSR ghost already paints the whole waterfall at full size with no entrance. When the harp mounts, layout(true, true) puts every line in mode 'in', so each one pops from scale 0.84 with a 6px blur. Meanwhile the ghost row fades on a slow-start ease-in-quad over 240ms (strum.css 198–202). For about 100–150ms each title is drawn twice: the full-size DOM copy plus a smaller, blurred canvas copy anchored at TEXT_X, with the right ends offset by up to about 15px on the big lines. The waterfall smears and re-enters on the frame Herb judges. With reduced motion the ghost cuts out instantly and the canvas fades in from alpha 0, which reads as a blink.
issues.fix: Make the ghost own the entrance and have the canvas continue it at the same phase. Add a CSS keyframe to .strum__ghost-row: opacity 0, scale(.84) and blur(6px) at 0%; scale(1.02) at 62%; none at 100%. Run it for 440ms with transform-origin 16px at the baseline and animation-delay var(--strum-delay). In the StrumHarp constructor, read the phase of the first ghost row, `const played = stage.querySelector('.strum__ghost-row')?.getAnimations()[0]?.currentTime ?? 0`, and set each line's modeAt = performance.now() - played. Lines whose animation has already finished start in mode 'shown'. Then drop the ghost-row opacity/filter transition and simply set visibility: hidden on data-live, because both copies are pixel-identical at that moment. Also match the ghost's small-line weight to the canvas: BODY_WEIGHT is 460 but the ghost uses --font-weight-meta (440). Set BODY_WEIGHT to 440, or read the token with getComputedStyle, so the swap shows no weight jump.

issues.problem: On iPhone, WebAudio follows the ring/silent switch by default. Most people carry their phone on silent, so every pluck, the chord and the chime are inaudible there. The piece looks like it has no sound on exactly the device the brief says must survive. Nothing in the code sets the audio session.
issues.fix: In unlock(), before creating or resuming the context, add: `if (navigator.audioSession && navigator.audioSession.type !== 'playback') navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback';` (Safari 16.4+). This lets WebAudio play past the silent switch. Do it inside the same user-gesture handler that already runs on pointerdown and touchend.

issues.problem: isResting requires !line.moving. So for the whole ratio change (a spring with ζ≈0.84 plus up to 330ms of stagger, about 0.6–0.8s), every line goes through drawLive: about 150 per-glyph fillText calls at a new fractional size each frame. That means fresh glyph rasterisation at up to 140px × DPR 2 on every frame, defeating the glyph cache. fontFor (line 1012) also throws away and rebuilds its font strings per line per frame because fontSize changes. The ratio change is the second half of the wow moment, it is followed straight away by the chord strum, and on a mid-range phone this is where frames drop.
issues.fix: Add a moving-but-silent path. When line.moving && energy === 0 && !held && flash === 0, blit the cache built at line.target, scaled by line.size / line.target about (TEXT_X, baseline) in blitLine: setTransform(scale*k*dpr, 0, 0, scale*k*dpr, …). The law tracking differs by a fraction of a pixel mid-spring, which is invisible, and the cache is rebuilt once when the spring settles. In ensureCache, key on line.target rather than line.size whenever line.moving. A ratio change then costs about 12 drawImage calls per frame.

issues.problem: While display lines ring (the intro, a strum, the chord), each glyph from 20px up gets a continuous per-frame rotation. Skia keys glyph strikes by the full matrix, so every distinct angle re-rasterises the glyph. That is about 60 large rotated glyph rasters per frame for the first 1–2 seconds after load and after every chord.
issues.fix: Quantise the tilt to a fixed step and zero the small angles: `const angle = Math.atan(slope); const snapped = Math.abs(angle) < 0.01 ? 0 : Math.round(angle / 0.0087) * 0.0087;` (0.5° steps). Build cos and sin from the snapped angle. Repeated angles across frames and glyphs then hit the strike cache, and the visual difference cannot be seen at 7Hz.

issues.problem: Strength is clamp(speed × 1.2, 0.15, 1) in px/ms, so any sweep faster than 0.83px/ms is full force. Ordinary mouse and finger sweeps run at 1–4px/ms, so nearly every strum is fortissimo with the same envelope width and weight swell. There are no dynamics, so the instrument cannot be played softly.
issues.fix: Use a log curve, for example `strength = clamp(0.12 + 0.42 * Math.log2(1 + speed), 0.15, 1)`. That gives about 0.36 at 0.5px/ms, 0.54 at 1px/ms and 1 at 3.7px/ms. A gentle pass then whispers and a flick slaps, and the visual and audio amplitudes follow together.

issues.problem: coarse comes from useSyncExternalStore with a server snapshot of false. On phones the hint hydrates as 'Click once for sound…' and MorphText then visibly morphs it into 'Tap once for sound…' right after load, which looks like a glitch on first view.
issues.fix: Render both strings and choose with CSS: two spans, toggled with @media (pointer: coarse) { [data-hint=pointer] { display: none } } and the reverse. Keep MorphText only for the locked-to-playing change, so hydration never morphs the copy.

issues.problem: Below 900px the stage has min-height 420px and touch-action none. On a landscape phone (about 375px tall), the page is taller than the viewport, and a touch anywhere on the stage cannot scroll it. The slider can only be reached by scrolling from the header strip.
issues.fix: Cap the stage height to the viewport: `.strum__stage { min-height: min(420px, calc(100dvh - 240px)); }` inside the 899px query. That keeps the page within one screen, and linesThatFit already shrinks the waterfall to match.

issues.problem: resize() returns early when the width and height are unchanged, so a devicePixelRatio change is ignored. That happens when the window is dragged from a 1x to a 2x display, or with browser zoom at the same CSS size, and the canvas stays at the old backing resolution, blurry or oversized.
issues.fix: Compare the DPR as well: `const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2); if (!initial && width === this.width && height === this.height && dpr === this.dpr) return;`. Also listen to matchMedia(`(resolution: ${dpr}dppx)`) change and call resize(false).

recheck.wowGap: Add sympathetic resonance, so the ratio can be seen as well as heard. When a string is plucked, every other present string whose frequency forms a simple ratio with it shivers faintly in response, its glyphs swelling slightly: near n/m with n, m ≤ 3, so octaves, fifths and fourths. The test runs on line.frequency (the voiced chord tones). For each other line, find the best small-integer match, set consonance = 1 / (n·m) when the cents error is under 15 and 0 otherwise, and strike it at strength 0.14 × consonance after 35ms. Emit a quiet voice at amplitude 0.06 × consonance with no pick noise, and skip it when the voice count is above 12. Plucking the 112px "Boys" at the octave ratio then makes the whole waterfall breathe with it. At the perfect fifth every other string answers. At the augmented fourth almost nothing does. Dragging the slider changes how alive the harp feels, with no explanation needed. That is the brief's thesis, "the ratio is the chord", made visible in the type itself.

build.summary: Sand is one of Herb's real recently played covers (the 640px imageLarge) set into a tall light tray as a crisp picture made of grains. Press and rub it and the grains under the brush come loose. They pour down the face of the cover and pile into a coloured dune on the floor. Following the engineer review's advice, the falling-sand simulation runs on the CPU: there are two layers, the picture mask and a moving sand layer, and grains are never created or lost. Each grain falls faster as it drops and slides off diagonally at random. The GPU only draws. One full-screen pass draws the cover with rounded corners wherever the picture is broken and draws each loose grain as a rounded bead. A second pass draws every grain in flight as its own small quad. Hold still for 640ms (a round-capped ring fills under the pointer), double-click, or press R, and every loose grain arcs back to its own spot. The flight lasts 700ms with a slight overshoot, starts with the grains nearest the press and spreads outward, and each grain shrinks and pops back as it lands. The tray then gives a small bounce and the phone buzzes. Next cover (→) uses the herb skeptic's upgrade: the picture collapses from the top down, and partway through the fall all the grains erupt and land as the next record. Grains are matched to new spots by brightness, and each grain changes colour in flight. The loose-grain count rolls on SlotNumber, the title and artist change with MorphText, and you can switch grain size between Fine, Sand and Gravel.
build.wowMoment: Crumble half a cover into a dune, then press →. The rest of the picture collapses from the top down, and partway through the fall about 15,000 grains erupt from the top of the sand. Each one arcs into a spot of matching brightness in the NEXT album, changing colour as it flies. The new record lands with a ripple of tiny pops and snaps back whole.
build.knownIssues: Never run in a real browser, as the rules required. What was checked: all three checks pass, plus eslint, and the type checker shows no entries for the folder. Two Node scripts in the scratchpad also exercised the logic. The first ran the grid on its own and showed no grains are lost, the dune settles at 45°, and a step takes about 0.15ms. The second ran SandField end to end with a fake WebGL context and fake DOM. It covered the intro bite, rubbing, the hold-to-rebuild ring, keyboard crumble, tap poke, the next-cover eruption, a grain-size change, reduced motion, and the loop going idle; the grain count stayed exact in the normal-motion run. The shaders have only passed the parse check. No real GLSL compiler ran, so on-GPU compile errors and the overall look are unverified. Departures from the brief: (1) Tilt and 8-direction gravity are cut, as both skeptics advised. (2) The simulation runs on the CPU instead of the GPU Margolus/RGBA8UI approach (engineer review). (3) The picture is a backdrop rather than a wall, because grains could never leave a bite surrounded by picture; crumbled sand falls in front of the cover. (4) The piles settle at a steady 45° rather than about 34°; the momentum spread barely changes the final slope. (5) Brushing needs a press on desktop, and hover only shows a ring cursor and the grain pattern under it (both skeptics). (6) Next cover erupts partway through the collapse, because a full collapse just fills the bottom of the tray as a solid block. (7) The layout is three columns at 900px and wider: title and controls on the left, track and count on the right. Below 900px it stacks. page.js now passes imageLarge. Simulated walkthrough:
- **Server render and mount:** No window access in the server render. The page server component falls back to /flyout covers if Spotify fails. Under StrictMode the field is created twice and destroyed once cleanly: the async start() checks `destroyed`, and timers and observers are cleared.
- **WebGL and shaders:** The WebGL2 API usage is correct: bufferSubData element counts, a stride/offset layout that obeys alignment, normalized UNSIGNED_BYTE colours, and texelFetch on RGBA8/R8 NEAREST textures. The state byte layout (homeX, homeY, kind) matches the shader decode. Cover loads use crossOrigin, and a 1px getImageData probe catches tainted images.
- **Simulation:** It runs on the CPU and goes idle once 30 steps pass with nothing moving.
- **Input:** The mouse brush only works while pressed, so hovering is non-destructive. Pointer capture is used for mouse and pen. Hold-still ring, tap poke, double-click and R all trigger.
- **Next cover:** The luminance-sorted re-homing is correctly encoded: count stays under 65536, and keys are exact in Float64.
- **Hidden tab and unmount:** Hidden tab and offscreen both stop the rAF loop. Unmount cleans up and calls loseContext.

No blockers found. The majors are a black flash whenever the canvas is resized, a simulation speed tied to frame rate, and grains freezing mid-air when an eruption starts mid-fall.

issues.problem: The governor's resize() runs after render(). Setting canvas.width clears the drawing buffer you just drew into, and with alpha:false that shows as an opaque black frame on a light page. If needsFrame() is false on that frame (dirty isn't part of needsFrame), the canvas stays black until the next interaction.
issues.fix: Sample the governor at the top of tick, before updatePointer, and call resize() before render(). Alternatively, call this.render(now) right after any resize. Also add `this.dirty` to needsFrame.

issues.problem: The ResizeObserver callback resizes the canvas, which clears it, then only calls wake(). The cleared buffer is painted that frame, so window drags and phone rotation flicker black on every frame.
issues.fix: In handleResize, call this.render(performance.now()) synchronously after this.resize(), whenever a grid exists and the context isn't lost.

issues.problem: STEPS_PER_FRAME is a fixed 2 per rAF. Sand falls twice as fast on 120Hz ProMotion as on 60Hz and slows down whenever frames drop. The cascade→erupt timing (ERUPT_AFTER_MS, which uses wall-clock time) therefore produces a different picture on each display.
issues.fix: Use a fixed-timestep accumulator: `this.simDebt += dt; while (this.simDebt >= 1000/120 && steps < 4) { stepGrid(); this.simDebt -= 1000/120; steps++ }`. That gives 120 steps/s at any refresh rate, and stillSteps should count real steps.

issues.problem: erupt() fires 760ms into the cascade, while most of the old cover is still a falling curtain. launch() stops stepGrid, so every grain with a delay up to 0.47s (ERUPT_DEPTH_S + SCATTER_S) hangs dead in mid-air until its turn. The result looks like a freeze-frame, not an eruption. Rebuild via the button, R or double-click right after a stroke freezes airborne grains the same way.
issues.fix: Wait to erupt until the cascade has fully released and the pile has settled: `elapsed >= CASCADE_MS + CASCADE_JITTER_MS && this.stillSteps >= 8`. Bump GRAVITY 1.6x during a cascade so the collapse still lands in about 900ms. For rebuild, either run the flight only when stillSteps is above a threshold, or pass each grain's velocity in aTiming.y and keep it falling in FLIGHT_VERTEX while since < 0.

issues.problem: `100cqh - 112px` subtracts the .sand padding a second time, because container query units already measure the content box. The same happens with `100cqw - 64px`, and at line 397 on mobile. In the 1280-wide judging iframe the tray comes out about 322px wide, so the grid is about 107 cells and the cover holds about 11k grains. The brief's '40,000 grains' wow lands at a quarter of its scale.
issues.fix: Use `min(calc(100cqh * 0.7), calc(100cqw - var(--sand-side) * 2 - 64px), 600px)` and on mobile `calc((100cqh - 188px) * 0.7)`. Consider DEFAULT_GRAIN 'fine' so a typical desktop tray reaches about 40k grains.

issues.problem: On the first frame of the eruption, erupt() does a lot of synchronous work. It runs sampleCells for the next cover (drawImage plus getImageData), sorts two 57k Float64 arrays, uploads a 512² texture and generates mipmaps, then calls bufferSubData for about 1.8MB. That costs roughly 10-20ms and drops a frame exactly at the wow moment.
issues.fix: Prepare the next cover in the background during the cascade, or as soon as ensureCover resolves. Pre-sample its cells, upload it into the hidden slot, and build the homeKeys sort ahead of time. erupt() then only needs the grain sort and the buffer upload.

issues.problem: When a flight lands, finishFlight swaps instantly from beads to the smooth photo. Flight beads are saturated 1.18x, ±5% shade, with light-coloured gaps. The intact picture is the plain 512 texture at lattice 0.07. The landing therefore reads as a hard texture-and-colour pop rather than grains fusing into the image.
issues.fix: Add a `this.fuse = { start }` and drive uLattice from 1.0 down to LATTICE_BASE over about 320ms with ease-out after landing. Keep requesting frames while it runs, so the beads melt into the picture.

issues.problem: A mipmapped `texture(uCover, ...)` is sampled inside a non-uniform branch (the picture texel test). Implicit derivatives are undefined along the eroded edges, which risks speckled or wrong-LOD pixels at the bite border on some GPUs.
issues.fix: Sample the cover once before the `if`, unconditionally, or use `textureLod(uCover, uv, 0.0)`. The cover is magnified at the shipped sizes anyway.

issues.problem: The hint reads 'Rub the cover to crumble it. Hold still to pull it back.' But a mouse hover does nothing and hold-still only counts while pressed, so a desktop judge hovering still waits forever. Double-click and R are only mentioned in the aria-label.
issues.fix: Use 'Drag across the cover to crumble it. Press and hold to pull it back.' (or 'double-click to pull it back').

issues.problem: The window-level ArrowRight and N shortcuts fire Next cover even while focus is in the Grain size radiogroup or on nav links, where an arrow key should move focus between options.
issues.fix: Skip the shortcut when event.target sits inside a `[role=radiogroup]` or a link, or only handle ArrowRight while the tray or document body has focus.

issues.problem: localPoint measures from the border-box rect, but the canvas and cellCss use the padding box, so the brush and ring sit 1px off along both axes.
issues.fix: Subtract the tray border: `event.clientX - rect.left - this.surface.clientLeft` and `event.clientY - rect.top - this.surface.clientTop`.

issues.problem: If the next cover's image never settles (a stalled request), the cascade waits on readyCover indefinitely. busy stays true, so both Rebuild and Next stay disabled for good.
issues.fix: Add a deadline. After ERUPT_AFTER_MS + 2500ms with no ready cover, call erupt(this.current, this.coverIndex), or fall back to the entry for LAST_RESORT.

issues.problem: If a Spotify image fails or is tainted, it silently becomes card-01, but the title and artist of the Spotify track still display under the wrong picture.
issues.fix: On fallback, return the cover with the title and artist cleared (or set to the local card's labels), or let ensureCover skip to the next index.

issues.problem: The track title uses --font-weight-emphasis (540) at text-ui. On the ladder, 540 is the 10px body weight, so it doesn't belong as title emphasis at this size.
issues.fix: Use the subsection weight token (550/560) for .sand__title, or drop the override and let the text-ui token weight carry it next to the secondary-ink artist.

issues.problem: The loading placeholder is always surface-sunken. sampleCells already computes `average`, but nothing uses it, so the brief's 'cover's average colour block' loading state is missing.
issues.fix: After loadCover resolves, set `--sand-average` on the tray from sampleCells(...).average and use it as the placeholder background. Load a 16px sample first if you want it before full decode.

issues.problem: FALLBACK_COVERS is duplicated verbatim in page.js and sandParams.js.
issues.fix: Import FALLBACK_COVERS from ./sandParams in page.js.

issues.problem: The error copy blames WebGL2 being switched off for every failure, including a shader compile or link error.
issues.fix: Use neutral copy such as 'This tray could not start its renderer.'

build.summary: Copier is a slit-scan photocopier drawn on one sheet. The light bar is the boundary: rows above it are the toner copy, and below it the colour original still sits live on the glass. Each frame the engine records the original's pose (position, angle, scale), timestamped from coalesced pointer events, into a 1280-row float "pose ledger" texture. Every new row the bar crosses gets the pose from the moment the light passed it, with rotation stored as an angle so fast twists don't tear. A raw WebGL2 fragment shader then rebuilds the copy from that ledger with toner thresholding, 1px edge fill, 1.5px grain, drum streaks along x, paper fibre, a 0.3° skew and a thin line along the original's edge. There are four presets: Xerox, a two-ink misregistered Riso, Fax with row banding, and blue-line Diazo. A finished pass holds for a moment, then the sheet drops 24px and flies on a 420ms / 0.18 spring into a tray that fans out. "Copy the copy" puts the latest sheet back on the glass and runs another pass. The generation counter rolls up, and each generation adds threshold creep, blur and stronger streaks, so the picture slowly turns into a black toner silhouette. Inputs: drag with inertia, wheel or two-finger twist and pinch, grab the bar to carry the scan yourself (it never goes backwards, and the motor ramps back in over 200ms), Space and Enter, arrow keys, and dropping in your own image. Rendering only loops while something moves, pauses when the tab is hidden or the sheet is off screen, steps its pixel ratio down on slow frames, and falls back to Canvas2D without WebGL2.
build.wowMoment: You don't have to touch anything for the first frame. Honus Wagner's card is already 56% copied, and the black-toner top half is bent into an S-curve, outline and all, because the original sways on the glass while the mint light bar keeps moving down. Cause and effect sit on one line. Then hit Enter a few times: each copy goes back on the glass, the Generation counter rolls up, and the face breaks down into a solid black toner silhouette.
build.knownIssues: Nothing was run in a browser, as the rules required; all three checks pass. To check the look I ported the shader to numpy (scratchpad copier_sim.py) and rendered the first frame, all four presets and six generations offline. They read as intended: an S-curved toner copy, Riso pink and blue, no dot screens. Still unverified at runtime: the DOM layout and CSS, the flight-to-tray landing alignment, two-finger twist on a real phone, the Canvas2D fallback, and the synthesised motor sound level. Choices to know about: I followed the engineer's upgrade and used one sheet with the bar as the boundary instead of two panes, so the brief's 640px platen-above-copy layout doesn't apply. The default original is the sharp 660px Wagner card; John, Paul and George are thumbnails and look soft on the platen because the source images are 200px. The `embedded` mode is not implemented, since lab pieces aren't embedded. Spotify covers are not used; you can drop in your own image instead. Only the last 6 copies keep full resolution, so older tray sheets can't go back on the glass. A wheel over the sheet rotates the picture instead of scrolling the page. Sound starts on the first gesture, can be turned off under "Tune the toner", and the scripted first pass is silent.

critique.firstFrame:

The canvas then fades in over 900ms on top of the fallback, which matches it pixel for pixel, so nothing jumps. The lid-edge line prints as a wavy rule. The bottom half is the full-colour card still swaying live on the grey glass, and a mint lamp line with a white core sits between them. From about 2.2s on, the hero stage is a plain colour card on grey with a faint line at the top. issues.problem: The finished copy is auto-ejected 950ms after the pass. The glass then goes back to a plain colour card on grey with no toner on it, so the wow is gone about 2.2s after load. Preset chips and toner dials also have no visible effect while idle, because nothing printed is on the glass. Clicking Riso changes only the chip.
issues.fix: Leave the finished copy on the glass in the 'hold' phase indefinitely and keep rendering it live through the shader, so presets and dials restyle it in place. Eject only on the next pointerdown, Space, Enter, or a source change. Move `renderer.bake` from finishPass to eject so the tray thumbnail matches the preset in use when the copy leaves.

issues.problem: When the autoplay pass ends, a visitor's first instinct is to drag the picture, but in the idle phase that prints nothing. The visitor has to find Copy or Space first, then drag, which splits the mechanic into two steps and delays the moment of cause and effect.
issues.fix: In onPointerDown, when `phase === 'idle'` and the press is on the picture, eject any held copy and call startPass() before taking the pointer. The first drag then prints immediately. Keep Space and Copy for hands-off passes.

issues.problem: In the desktop grid (container wider than 960px), the sheet width comes only from viewport height. On a tall, medium-width box, such as a 1024x1366 iPad in portrait or a 1100x1000 window, the minimum track sum is 208+688+148+112+64 = 1220px. That is wider than the container, and with `justify-content: center` plus `overflow-x: clip` the head/panel column and the tray get clipped on both sides.
issues.fix: Set the sheet size on `.copier__layout`, where cqw resolves against `.copier`: `--copier-sheet-h: min(clamp(360px, calc(100dvh - 136px), 860px), calc((100cqw - 552px) * 1.25));`. Alternatively, raise the stacking breakpoint to `@container (max-width: 1220px)`.

issues.problem: The DPR cap tests `cssWidth < 640`, which is the sheet width, not the viewport width. The sheet is under 640px on almost every laptop (viewport heights below about 936px), so Retina MacBooks render at DPR 1.5, which then gets upscaled. That softens exactly the toner grain, edge fill and streak detail the piece depends on.
issues.fix: Key the cap off the device instead: `const cap = window.matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches || window.innerWidth < 640 ? 1.5 : 2;`.

issues.problem: If the tab is hidden or the sheet scrolls offscreen mid-pass, resume() cancels rAF but leaves the motor noise and hum gains at their pass level. The AudioContext keeps running, so the copier keeps droning in the background tab until the visitor returns. The context is also never suspended while idle.
issues.fix: In resume(), when `!visible || !onscreen`, call `sound.drive(0)`. Give createCopierSound a `sleep()` that runs `context.suspend()` (and `resume()` from wake()). Call it on hidden and on entering idle, and call wake() again when a pass starts.

issues.problem: Every frame re-runs the full toner shader over the whole printed area: 5 to 10 textureLod taps, 4-octave fbm1, 4-octave fbm2 paper and noise2, about 1.9M px at DPR 2. Yet only the band of about 8 rows above the lamp has changed. The brief planned a cached print target, and `preserveDrawingBuffer: true` (line 56) adds a buffer copy every frame for no benefit.
issues.fix: Bake the toner pass into an RGBA8 print target band by band, using a scissor on [prevRow, row) and recomputing the whole target only when params or the preset change. Composite that texture plus the live platen in the display pass. Drop preserveDrawingBuffer, since bake reads from its own FBO.

issues.problem: Eject stacks three synchronous main-thread jobs on one frame: a 5MB readPixels with a new ImageData (from finishPass), a 1024x1280 to 384x480 JPEG toDataURL in makeThumb, and a 1216x1520 flight canvas at DPR 2 that is bigger than the sheet itself. The first frames of the spring flight can hitch.
issues.fix: Use the 1024x1280 sheet canvas, or an ImageBitmap of it, as the flight node directly and scale it with CSS instead of redrawing it at DPR. Build the thumbnail with `createImageBitmap(sheet, {resizeWidth: 384})` after the flight lands. Reuse one ImageData in CopierGL.bake.

issues.problem: The wheel handler always calls preventDefault. In the stacked layout (960px and below), where the page scrolls, a trackpad scroll that passes over the sheet is captured and rotates the picture. It also kills the scripted sway.
issues.fix: Only capture the wheel when ctrlKey or metaKey is held, or while the pointer is inside the original (`insideOriginal(event.clientX, event.clientY)`). Otherwise let the page scroll.

issues.problem: Below 960px the tray sits under the panel, off the bottom of the screen. Ejected copies fly off the bottom edge to a pile the visitor cannot see, and the Copies count and Copy the copy are far from the glass.
issues.fix: In the stacked layout, put a compact tray row (count plus the top 3 sheets at 48px) directly under the sheet, before the panel, so the eject lands on screen.

issues.problem: Each arrow key adds 0.5*pxPerCss sheet px/ms of velocity, about 500 css px/s, which coasts roughly 120px with a 240ms tau and accumulates on key repeat. That is a shove, not a nudge.
issues.fix: Use `(event.shiftKey ? 0.24 : 0.08) * k` and cap the speed with `velocity.x = clamp(velocity.x, -1.2*k, 1.2*k)` (and the same for y).

issues.problem: The `[data-near]` rule comes after `[data-dragging]` and has the same specificity. If the drag starts near the bar, the cursor shows ns-resize while the visitor is actually dragging the picture.
issues.fix: Add `.copier-sheet[data-dragging="true"][data-near="true"] { cursor: grabbing; }`, or call setNear(0) in onPointerDown when taking the picture path.

issues.problem: The ledger texture starts as zeros. With reduced motion, the first pass starts from row 0, and while scan is between 0.4 and 1, ledgerAt reads row 0 with pose.w = 0. That divides by zero in toLocal, so the top pixel row renders NaN garbage for a few frames.
issues.fix: After creating it, initialise the ledger with identity poses (x=W/2, y=H/2, angle 0, scale 1), or use `max(pose.w, 1e-3)` in toLocal and the lod calculation.

issues.problem: The 'The tray is empty' label in a sunken box repeats 'Copies 0' directly above it. Herb's taste bans micro-labels that explain what is already visible.
issues.fix: Remove the text and leave a quiet sunken 4:5 slot, or a hairline outline, as the empty pile.

issues.problem: The Space and Enter key hints show on phones, where there is no keyboard, and widen the two action buttons.
issues.fix: Hide `.copier-kbd` under `@media (pointer: coarse)`.

issues.problem: The file input is visually hidden but still tabbable. When it takes keyboard focus, no ring appears, because `:focus-visible` targets the label and not the input.
issues.fix: Add `.copier-link:has(.copier-file:focus-visible) { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }`.

issues.problem: `--copier-lamp` and `--copier-ease-carriage` are defined but never used. They are leftover slop.
issues.fix: Delete both custom properties.

critique.wowGap: Make the glass never idle. When a pass finishes, leave the copy on the glass, still rendered live by the shader, instead of auto-ejecting it after 950ms. Then the vote frame stays up, and the preset chips and toner dials restyle the copy visibly in place. The visitor's next touch does the rest: grabbing the picture, Space or Enter bakes and lifts the sheet into the tray and starts the next pass at once. Every drag then prints, and every print ends in the satisfying lift-off into the tray.

changes: copierEngine.js: the finished copy now stays on the glass in 'hold' indefinitely, still drawn live by the shader, so the preset chips and dials restyle it in place. The HOLD_MS auto-eject is gone, and the loop sleeps once the glow, fresh fade and sway have settled.

copierEngine.js: the bake moved from finishPass into eject(). The tray sheet now matches whatever preset is in use when it leaves. eject() also starts a quick 240ms lamp return when a pass is queued (QUICK_RETURN_MS in copierMotion.js replaces HOLD_MS).

copierEngine.js: in onPointerDown, pressing in hold or return, or pressing on the picture while idle, ejects the held copy and starts a pass before it takes the pointer, so the first drag prints. It also calls setNear(0), which fixes the ns-resize cursor during a picture drag. Space and Copy still run hands-off passes.

copierEngine.js: the DPR cap now keys off the device: (pointer: coarse) or innerWidth < 640 gets 1.5, everything else gets 2.

copierEngine.js: resume() calls sound.drive(0) and sound.sleep() when the tab is hidden or the sheet is offscreen, and rouses the sound on return if a pass is running. Entering hold or idle puts the sound to sleep, and startPass rouses it.
