build.summary: Herb's recently played covers hang as a Calder mobile from one thread at the top of the page. Seven bent-steel arms with knots at the pivots are drawn on a single Canvas2D layer, and the covers are DOM buttons positioned with transforms written straight from the loop. Under it is a 2D rigid-body XPBD solver (mobileSim.js): 16 substeps, 5 alternating passes over the threads, threads that go slack (drawn sagging when they do), and a grab constraint tied to the exact point you hold, with a force cap so threads can't stretch. Each thread is tied at the arm's true balance point, computed bottom-up from the masses below it. A seeded tilt is then applied, and tilts that would make covers overlap are relaxed, so the mobile rests at Calder's slight angles and never collides (checked with 39 seeds across 9 box sizes). The layout zig-zags on tall phone screens. On load the mobile is lowered folded over 1100ms, then gravity unfolds it. Pull, fling or brush past a cover: the pointer acts as wind, and a fling or fast brush turns covers on their threads until they flip to a mesh back in the album's colours, then unwind. Tapping a cover flies it up to the top arm while the top cover drops into its place, the cascade tips under the shifting weight and settles again, and the 30s preview plays. The thread hums with the music, and when a preview ends the next cover is promoted automatically. There is a Tune panel (wind, air damping, gravity, cover count, rehang seed) with rolling SlotNumber readouts, plus keyboard controls: Tab, arrows to nudge, Enter to play, Space for a gust. Reduced motion is handled, and the loop sleeps when idle, hidden or offscreen.
build.wowMoment: Tap the little cover at the bottom: it lifts off its hook and arcs up to the top arm while the big top cover drops past it. While they're in the air the whole cascade lurches under the lost weight. They land with a thump, the knots slide along the wires to new balance points, and the sculpture rocks into a new balance as the song starts. A faint hum shakes the thread it hangs from.

critique.firstFrame: Server paint: a light, empty ground with the "Mobile" heading and a one-line instruction at bottom left, and at bottom right the ink play button with "Title · Artist" and 0:00 / 0:30 in SlotNumber. Both blocks rise in with a 6px blur over 600ms. Once hydration finishes, the stage chunk mounts. The anchor thread and a folded fan of 8 arched wires (55° fold) come down from above the top edge over 1100ms on the entrance curve. Covers stay invisible until each 640px Spotify image decodes, then focus-pull in (scale 0.84 to 1, blur 6 to 0, 440ms) while the mobile is still descending. At 1.1s the fan opens under gravity. My headless renders show it overlapping like a fanned deck at first, spreading in about 2s and settling about 3s later. It lands as a down-right staircase: a 263px top cover on the left stepping down to 78px on the right at 1440x900. On a 390x844 phone it is a tidy six-cover zig-zag from 106px to 63px. At rest, covers 3/4 and 5/6 nearly touch (about 2px gap), so the desktop silhouette reads a little like a bar chart. Ambient yaw keeps it breathing (up to 88px of cover drift on desktop) for 30s after the last interaction, then it freezes still.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate cover-mobile: PASS. 2. compile-check cover-mobile: PASS (9 modules). 3. glsl-check: no shaders found (none in the piece; skipped as allowed). I also ran mobileLayout and mobileSim headlessly in node. Rest pose is stable (under 0.5px drift over 10s, no NaN). Thread stretch stays under 2px even on a 3600px/s fling. After a hard pull the mobile returns to its exact rest balance, but it takes 16 to 19s to get under 2px of residual sway, not the brief's 8s. During a promote the top arm tips 37° on desktop and 64° on phone, and lower arms up to 79°. Dragging a cover past the chain's reach makes the light arms reverse direction frame to frame (5 to 9° second differences).

issues.problem: Cover z-indices leak above the chrome. `.cm` is a stacking context (container-type gives it layout containment) and `.cm-stage` creates none, so covers at z 1+slot (4 to 8), the 40+ waiting covers and the 60+ flying covers sit above `.cm-player` (z 3) and `.cm-panel` (z 4). A swing, drag or promote flight passes over the play button, the caption and the open Tune panel, and steals their clicks.
issues.fix: Add `isolation: isolate; z-index: 0;` to `.cm-stage` so every cover layer is contained below the chrome.

issues.problem: Auto-advance ping-pongs between two songs. `promoteNext` always calls `promote(1)`, which swaps slots 0 and 1. When A ends, B goes to the top and A drops to slot 1. When B ends, A comes back. The jukebox loops two tracks forever and never reaches covers 3 to 8.
issues.fix: Keep a play cursor in the engine: `promoteNext` promotes `slots.indexOf(nextUnplayedCoverIndex)`, cycling 1 → 2 → … → n-1 by cover play order. Or promote the slot holding the most recently played cover's successor in the `covers` array.

issues.problem: A held cover keeps its slot z-index (1+slot). Grabbing the big top cover (z 1) and dragging it through the cascade passes it BEHIND every smaller cover, the opposite of the hand-held object coming toward you. There is also no press feedback beyond the cursor change.
issues.fix: In placeCover, use layer 50 for `pointer.coverIndex` while `pointer.mode === 'grab'`. Kick `popVelocity[coverIndex] += POP_KICK * 0.4` on grab start for a tiny press-lift. Restore 1+slot on release.

issues.problem: The player button never wakes the sleeping engine. After about 40s idle the rAF loop has stopped (quietFor > SLEEP_HOLD). Tapping play on a phone, or pressing it by keyboard, starts the audio, but no frame runs, so there is no thread hum and no ambient sway while the music plays. `playing` only keeps the loop alive once a frame is already running.
issues.fix: Expose `wake: touch` on the controller from mountMobile and call `controllerRef.current?.wake()` in handleToggle, handlePromote and handleTopTap. Better still, wake from the player's 'play' event inside createPreviewPlayer's onChange.

issues.problem: `play()` awaits the iTunes lookup (`resolveUrl`) before calling `audio.play()`. On iOS Safari the user gesture does not survive a slow, uncached fetch, so the first tap on a cover is silent (NotAllowedError, quietly reset to idle). Prefetch only starts on Root pointerenter, which on touch is the same tap.
issues.fix: Call `audio.play()` synchronously inside the gesture: either play a tiny silent data-URI to unlock the element, then swap src and play after the lookup, or start prefetch on mount (idle callback) for the hung covers so the URL is usually cached and `audio.src` can be set before any await.

issues.problem: Dragging a cover beyond what the thread chain can reach makes the grab force cap fight the hard threads, and the light arms (mass 0.012 to 0.06) chatter. Measured: top cover pulled down 300px at 1440x900 gives an arm reversing direction 9 of 28 frames with 8.7° second differences. Bottom cover pulled down 250px on a phone gives 11 of 28 reversals. This is the 'pull it down hard' wow gesture, and the wires buzz instead of stretching cleanly.
issues.fix: In moveGrab, clamp the target to the reachable radius from the anchor: precompute the sum of thread, arm-half and cover-tie lengths along the path to the grabbed slot, then project the target onto that circle. Also add grab velocity damping (blend body velocity toward pointer velocity, about 0.15 per substep) so the compliant constraint cannot ring.

issues.problem: Settle is about twice as long as the brief. After a hard pull and release, max cover displacement is still 11 to 17px at 8s and only drops under 2px at 16 to 19s. The tail is a low-amplitude wobble rather than a finished settle.
issues.fix: Add knot friction instead of more air damping, so big swings keep their weight. In the substep velocity update, apply extra angular damping only when |omega| is small (e.g. omega *= exp(-h / 0.6) when |omega| < 0.15 rad/s), or damp each arm's angular velocity relative to its parent. Tune for under 2px at 8s.

issues.problem: The collision-aware tilt search only requires 5% of the top cover size as a gap. At 1440x900, covers 3/4 and 5/6 rest about 2px apart, so the cascade looks cramped and accidental in the first frame.
issues.fix: Raise the margin to about 0.16 × sizes[0]. Let the search also stretch the cover thread (coverThread ±30%) and not only flip or shrink tilts, so each cover gets clear air.

issues.problem: Ambient yaw switches off 30s after the last interaction and the sculpture freezes dead still, usually while Herb is still looking at it. A Calder mobile reads as alive because it never fully stops.
issues.fix: Keep a floor of ambient 0.25 while visible and not reduced-motion, so drift continues at low amplitude. The sim is cheap (about 13 threads × 80 iterations); still pause on hidden or offscreen.

issues.problem: `sides` starts at 0 on every mount, but the button may still carry data-side="back" from the previous engine (remount on count, seed or breakpoint change). A cover flipped at that moment keeps showing its mesh back while facing front.
issues.fix: Use `new Int8Array(total).fill(-1)` so the first placeCover always writes data-side.

issues.problem: Any change to count (the Covers slider, or crossing 640px when resizing or rotating) remounts the engine. mountMobile always calls build(true), so the full 1100ms drop replays, once per slider step.
issues.fix: Pass `withEntrance` from a ref that is true only on first mount (or a seed change), and use build(false) plus a small gust for count and breakpoint remounts.

issues.problem: In a hidden tab rAF is paused, so a promote's flights never finish. The next preview end calls promote(1), which bails because `state.flights.length > 0`, and background listening stops after two tracks.
issues.fix: In promote, if `document.hidden`, swap slots, call setHookEmpty(false) and retargetPivots immediately without queuing flights.

issues.problem: A second finger's pointerdown overwrites `pointer.id` and the grab body while the first finger is still holding a cover, so the first finger's grab is silently dropped mid-drag.
issues.fix: Return early from onPointerDown when `pointer.id !== null`.

issues.problem: Tab order follows the covers array, not the hanging order. After a few promotes, Tab jumps around the sculpture.
issues.fix: When slots change, set `element.style.order`, or reassign tabIndex so that it follows slot order. Simplest: in setSlotLook, reorder the DOM via `container.append(element)` in slot order after each landing.

issues.problem: setPlayback runs once a second during playback and re-renders the whole tree, including MobileStage and its 8 buttons with fresh inline ref callbacks.
issues.fix: Wrap MobileStage in React.memo (all props are already stable), and move the player readout into its own component that subscribes to the snapshot.

issues.problem: Long 'Title · Artist' captions are hard-clipped mid-glyph (nowrap and overflow hidden, with no fade). The fallback content also reads 'Card 01 · Local scans', which is placeholder slop.
issues.fix: Add a multi-stop mask-image fade on the right edge of `.cm-player__title`. Give the fallback covers real titles from /flyout's CREDITS.md.

critique.wowGap: Lift the held cover. While it is grabbed, raise it to the front (z 50), give it a small spring press-lift (pop up to about 1.04), and clamp the drag target to the chain's reach so the wires pull straight instead of buzzing. The brief's wow gesture is pulling the smallest cover down hard. Right now a grabbed top cover slides behind the smaller ones and the arms chatter once the chain goes taut. build.summary: One line is a phone-width music app (Home, Search, Library, Liked, Profile) whose tab indicator is a single ink thread. Each of the five icons is one continuous stroke, authored close to Lucide's proportions, with both ends at the bottom: the house is entered through its door, the magnifier through its handle, the heart at its tip, and the person and the books at their base. Every tap builds an arc-length track at runtime: the old icon's stroke, an exit fillet, a rail that runs between the icons and their labels with 6px corners, a riser, then the new icon's stroke. Head and tail ride that track on separate springs (260/24 and 170/22, tail held for 50ms), so the old icon unthreads stroke by stroke as the new one is stitched in. The line is drawn on a DPR-capped canvas as a variable-width ribbon with round caps: an underdamped width spring keyed to rest length over current length makes it go taut and thin in flight, then bulge past its rest width as it lands. Label weight runs from 490 to 590 with how much of each icon is covered. Icons the thread passes under dip with a small spring. Interrupting mid-flight retraces or rethreads along the existing body. Dragging pulls the head 1:1 under the intermediate icons and rubber-bands at the edges. On release the head's position is projected 120ms ahead and snapped to a tab. The panel title morphs through MorphText. Real Spotify covers slide 24px in the direction of travel and depixelate 8×8 → 16 → 32 → full with a 30ms stagger.
build.wowMoment: Grab the Library icon and drag right. The tail unpicks the books one spine at a time while the thread thins to a hair along the rail, and each icon it passes under dips as it goes by. Let go and it snaps into the nearest tab: the thread threads up through the heart's tip, the label goes from 490 to 590 as the outline fills, and the line fattens for a beat as the tail lands.

The card holds a 3×2 grid of grey surface-sunken squares with titles and artists, and below it a five-tab bar of thin grey 1.5px icons. On hydration the engine sets data-live and writes weight 490 to every label, so Home un-bolds and the tab looks unselected for about 360ms. The card then rises through a 6px blur. 2. compile-check printed "PASS  compile one-line (6 modules)".

I also ran the engine headless in Node, using copies of LineTrain.js and oneLineIcons.js in the scratchpad with a stubbed canvas, labels and rAF. Across the intro, taps (including interrupted taps), drag forward and back, flick and hover:

- Labels finished at exactly "wght" 590 on the active tab and 490 on the rest, so on the weight ladder.

- Dragging back past the icon flipped into the left rubber-band stub as intended.
