Icon lengths: home 90.6px, search 65.8px, library 117.1px, liked 70.2px, profile 61.9px.

issues.problem: The stitch-in can't be read. With head stiffness 260 and no speed shaping, the head reaches roughly 2000px/s on the rail. In the simulation, Home→Profile entered the icon at frame 10 and finished tracing it at frame 14, so the profile stroke is sewn in 4 frames (67ms). Home→Search took 7 frames. The brief's moment of the line threading itself into the new icon is a blur on every tap. About 55 more frames of nearly invisible scale and tug settling follow.
issues.fix: Shape head speed by track region. While state.head is past track.iconStart and below track.length (the target icon span), clamp headVelocity to about layout.iconLength[goal] / 0.2 px/s after each substep, or switch to a softer sewing spring (around stiffness 90, damping 19) once the head crosses iconStart. The rail run stays whip-fast, and the icon is visibly traced stroke by stroke over about 200ms.

issues.problem: Two problems with the covers. (1) useCovers waits on Promise.all for every cover, up to 30 images, so all six tiles stay grey until the slowest image loads. On a phone that is seconds of empty grid in the first frame. (2) If any image fails, useCovers filters it out, loaded.get() returns undefined, the effect exits early, data-ready is never set, and the tile stays a blank grey square forever. The brief's 'Error: fallback covers' state does not exist on the client.
issues.fix: Load per tile: in CoverTile create the Image (crossOrigin='anonymous') from cover.image in the effect and draw the pixel steps on its onload. On onerror, set data-ready on .ol-cover with the pixel canvases skipped, so .ol-cover__art shows the background image, or swap in a /flyout card. Then useCovers in OneLineExperience is not needed at all.

issues.problem: The Home label flashes on hydration. The SSR rule `.ol-bar:not([data-live]) .ol-tab[data-active] .ol-tab__label` makes Home 590 with full ink. On mount OneLineBar sets data-live immediately, and renderStill writes weight 490 and --ol-cov 0 to every label because the intro hasn't drawn yet. Home un-bolds for 360ms or more, then re-bolds as the intro lands.
issues.fix: Delete the :not([data-live]) bold rule so the server frame matches the pre-intro frame, with the label bolding only as the thread lands. Alternatively, set data-live inside startIntro rather than at mount, and skip writeLabels in renderStill while state.introPending is true.

issues.problem: The intro barely demonstrates the mechanic. Home is the leftmost tab, so the thread enters at x=-16 and runs only about 65px of rail before climbing into the house. It never passes under another icon, so first-time viewers never see the stretch-thin or tug behaviour.
issues.fix: Start the intro from the far edge instead: track.push(layout.width + 16, RAIL_Y), track.heading = Math.PI, routeToGoal(track, layout, target, -1). The thread then runs under Profile, Liked, Library and Search, tugging each, thins under tension, and stitches the house, all in the 900ms the brief asked for.

issues.problem: A release that snaps back makes a zero-radius hairpin. If the projected nearest tab is behind the head, rebuildToward copies the track up to the head with heading 0, and routeToGoal's else branch flips dir and sets the heading to π on the spot. The head keeps its positive along-track velocity from dragVelocity, so it instantly whips backward over its own body on the rail line, with no momentum carry or turn.
issues.fix: In go() with release=true, compare the new track.railDir with the rail direction before the rebuild. If they differ, set state.headVelocity = -Math.abs(state.headVelocity) * 0.25 so the head brakes before running back. Alternatively, route the reversal as a RAIL_RADIUS U-turn dipping 6px below the rail so the fold reads as a loop.

issues.problem: In dragMove, `floor = ... : state.tail + 2` takes over once the tail has fully left the source icon. If the finger retreats faster than the tail spring backs up, the head pins to tail+2 and throws away the rest of the finger delta. The line collapses to a dot and stops tracking the finger 1:1, which breaks the 'head moves 1:1 with the finger' rule for quick back-and-forth tugging.
issues.fix: Use `const floor = track.restEnd >= 0 ? track.restEnd : 0.5;` and let integrate's existing clamp (tail ≤ head − 0.5, tail velocity limited to the head's) shove the tail back. The head then always follows the finger, and the body bunches physically.

issues.problem: Panel titles are fixed strings (Recently played, Recent searches, Albums, Liked songs, On repeat). The brief asked for real artist and track names, such as '<artist> radio'. Every tab shows the same 3×2 cover grid shifted by an offset, so Search doesn't look like search. The server fallback reads 'Card 01 / Local scans', which looks like placeholder text.
issues.fix: Derive titles from the data, for example ICONS[1].title becomes `${covers[offset].artist} radio` or 'More like ' + artist, passed through MorphText so the artist name morphs. Give the fallback covers real titles and artists from the /flyout card metadata. Optionally render Search as rows (cover thumbnail plus query text) to vary the panels.

issues.problem: Profile icon: the neck curves arrive vertically at (12,11), but the head circle starts there with a horizontal tangent. The result is two 90° corners and a pointed Λ neck under the head. At 28px with round joins this can read as scribbly, which is the risk both skeptic reviews flagged.
issues.fix: Enter the head tangentially. Start the circle at angle π/2 + 0.5 and end it at π/2 − 0.5 (or the reverse), and aim the neck cubics at those points with matching tangents, so the stroke flows shoulder → neck → around the head → neck → shoulder without cusps. Check it at 1× DPR.

issues.problem: The canvas backing size is only recomputed in the ResizeObserver callback. Dragging the window to a monitor with a different devicePixelRatio leaves the line blurry or oversized until the bar's width changes.
issues.fix: Add a matchMedia(`(resolution: ${window.devicePixelRatio}dppx)`) change listener that calls engine.resize(bar.offsetWidth) and re-arms itself, and remove it in cleanup.

issues.problem: Only one exiting panel is kept. On a second tap within 200ms, the panel that was still fading out unmounts abruptly, and the previous enter panel jumps from its enter animation into ol-panel-out, so the grid pops.
issues.fix: Keep a small array of exiting panels keyed by sequence, each removed on its own animationend. Alternatively, debounce panel commits until the line passes the tab, which already happens on release.

critique.wowGap: Make the stitch-in readable on every tap. Today the head reaches about 2000px/s on the rail and traces the whole target icon in 3–7 frames (Home→Profile takes 4 frames, 67ms), so "threads itself into the new one" is never actually seen. Give the head a separate sewing phase. Once state.head passes track.iconStart, clamp its along-track speed to about iconLength/0.2s, or hand it to a softer spring around stiffness 90 and damping 19. The cable still whips across thin and taut, then visibly slows and sews the icon in stroke by stroke over about 200ms, with the label weight climbing as each stroke lands. Pair it with an intro that enters from the right edge and runs under all four other tabs before sewing the house, so the first frame shows the whole mechanic.

build.summary: Scorch treats Herb's recently played covers as a stack of paper sheets, and the artwork itself is the fuel. A raw WebGL2 heat-and-fuel simulation runs in a ping-pong state texture (384² on desktop, 256² on phones; RGBA32F where the device supports it, otherwise RGBA16F with a minimum-step guard). Each cover's fuel comes from its own ink and saturation, rescaled per cover with CPU percentiles, so the dark lettering ignites at low heat and burns about 7× faster than bare paper. Hold still for 320ms and a ring charges, blooms and lights a hot spot that grows with easeOutBack; dragging becomes local wind that pushes the heat ahead or blows the front out. Esc or Douse kills the heat, → burns through to the next sheet, and at 92% burnt the scraps burn away through the same ramp and the cover underneath becomes the sheet with no visible jump. The display pass draws toast, umber, an orange ember line, crackled char with ash specks, a 1px char lip and the next cover through the hole, plus glow from a blurred heat texture, 4-tap rotated-grid edge antialiasing and paper grain. Around it are a Swiss side column with the title, presets (Paper, Board, Newsprint, Fuse), five sliders whose readouts roll, a burnt percentage that rolls, captions that blur in, a fuse-line loader, a capsule cursor that stretches with drag speed and shows the fuel under the pointer, synthesised crackle audio, and error, empty and reduced-motion states.
build.wowMoment: Light the black lettering or a dark shape and the ember line races along the ink like a lit fuse. I checked this in a CPU copy of the same sim: a thin ink line burns end to end in about 2–3s, then the fire jumps to joined shapes while the pale paper around them only toasts and is left standing as islands, with the next cover showing through the burnt-out type. The first frame already shows this: before the fade-in it runs 1.8s of burn from the two highest-fuel spots in the lower left, so the plate opens with ragged ember holes and the next cover's colours showing through.
build.knownIssues: Never run in a browser, as the brief required: verification was the three checks (all pass), a trace through the code by hand, and a CPU copy of the sim and display shader in the scratchpad that renders PNG frames, which I used to tune every constant. GPU behaviour should closely match that copy but has not been seen on screen. The live loop keeps the brief's 20-frame readback cadence but reads a 16×16 stats target rather than a 1×1 mip. Ember glow comes from a blurred 64² heat texture rather than a mip-bias-3 sample, to avoid needing generateMipmap on float targets. The ember line sits at the outer edge of the burn, between toast and char, with char and a dark lip at the hole. That is a deliberate change from the brief's band (b 0.62 to 0.9), because the CPU previews read more like real burning paper this way. Wind and the hold-to-ignite ring are untested on real touch hardware. The plate uses touch-action: none, so on phones the page scrolls only from the header and panel. Sound is on by default and starts at the first press; there is a toggle in the panel. The first sheet keeps burning by itself after load and turns over at 92%; covers with large pale areas can leave paper islands that stop short of 92%, and then → moves on. In Fuse mode bare paper never burns, so turnover usually needs →.

critique.firstFrame: Server render: the paper-coloured plate, with a fuse line creeping along its bottom edge as the loader, and the caption title. The '% burnt' readout stays hidden until the piece is ready. Once covers decode and the 1.8s pre-sim runs (4 heavy frames at 384², 2 at 256²), the canvas fades in from 12px blur. The cover underneath is the 300px Spotify image (images[1]), stretched to as much as 1520 device px, so it looks soft. Two burns start at the darkest blurred spots in the lower left. I ran a CPU copy of the sim at the real grid sizes (scratchpad/scorch-review/sim.mjs), and on a dark-backed cover the pre-sim alone has already burned 18-35% into holes, because ink fronts move about 0.25 UV/s. The result is one big hole showing the next cover, not two small ragged bites. The ember band and the toast halo look right on the light page. The fire then keeps going with no input, because paper sustains itself at about 0.03 UV/s. A mixed cover reaches 92% at about 20s and an all-dark one at about 4s, then turns over by itself to a fresh cover that does nothing. The visitor never gets to light the black lettering on sheet one, because the intro already used up the darkest spots.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate scorch: PASS. 2. compile-check scorch: PASS (9 modules). 3. glsl-check: all 6 shader programs ok (scorchShader.js:1, 10, 67, 131, 154, 178). Plain strings, no interpolation. I also ran a CPU replica of SCORCH_SIM (scratchpad/scorch-review/sim.mjs) to measure the real spread: ink front about 0.25 UV/s, paper about 0.03 UV/s, paper self-sustains at thresholdBase 0.32 and stops between 0.42 and 0.5.

issues.problem: The intro lights the two darkest spots (introSpots, from analysis.spots) and runs 1.8s of pre-sim. Paper self-sustains at thresholdBase 0.32, so sheet one burns itself up with no input: about 4s on dark covers, about 20s on mixed ones. On dark-backed art the first frame already has a 20-35% hole. The wow moment, lighting the ink yourself and watching it race, is used up before the visitor touches anything.
issues.fix: Light the intro at a low-fuel spot on the lower-left edge, not at the darkest spots: pick the minimum blurred fuel within u<0.3, v<0.3. Shorten presimSeconds to 1.2. Add an intro limiter: when readStats sees burnt > 0.12 and no user source has fired yet, call douse() so the bite freezes with its stain halo. Then raise SIM.thresholdBase to about 0.40 in scorchParams.js. That makes bare paper marginal (it creeps and dies unless fanned) while ink still catches below 0.1.

issues.problem: covers use track.image, which spotifyRecent sets to images[1], a 300x300 thumbnail. It is shown at up to 760 CSS px x DPR 2, a 5x upscale, so the artwork, which is both the fuel and the subject, looks blurry.
issues.fix: Use image: track.imageLarge ?? track.image. That is the 640px asset already returned by getRecentTracks. Use the same image for the caption still.

issues.problem: Blowing a front out against the wind cannot happen. Wind only moves heat by semi-Lagrangian advection, which conserves it, and the oxygen term makes burning up to 1.6x faster. A headwind just pushes heat back into burnt cells, and the heat diffuses back once the wind decays (tau 0.8s). The brief's 'drag against it to blow it out' and the smoke-stain halo never appear.
issues.fix: In SCORCH_SIM, take the burn gradient g from the 4 neighbours' .r (sample uState at vUv±texel). Compute head = max(0, dot(wind, normalize(g + 1e-5))) * step(1e-3, length(g)), which is wind blowing back into the burnt side. Multiply heat by exp(-uWindCool * head * uDt) with uWindCool about 6, and apply the oxygen boost only when dot(wind, g) < 0, which is a tailwind.

issues.problem: If the under cover fails to load (Spotify CORS or 404), tryStart and turnOver still accept status 'failed' as underIndex. turnOver then sets sheetIndex to the failed slot, and writeFuel reads slot.data.crop where data is null. The TypeError aborts the frame part-way through a turnover: onSheet never fires, so the caption goes stale, and the sheet becomes blank paper burning on the previous cover's fuel map.
issues.fix: In turnOver, call sheetIndex = usableFrom(underIndex) and continue only if slotFor(sheetIndex).status === 'ready', otherwise keep finishing and wait. In tryStart, wait until under is 'ready' or re-resolve it with usableFrom. Guard writeFuel with if (!slot.data) return.

issues.problem: trimSlots keeps only sheetIndex..+2. After failed covers are skipped, underIndex can be +3 or more. Its texture is then deleted and its status reset to idle, and prefetch never requests it again. The next finish waits forever for a 'ready' that never comes: finishing stays true and rAF runs at 60fps indefinitely.
issues.fix: Add keep.add(positionOf(underIndex)) in trimSlots and request(underIndex) in prefetch.

issues.problem: The under cover gets up to 22% soot darkening and an ember tint from the state's glow. At the end of a finish the whole plate shows the under cover still sooted, then turnOver clears the state and it snaps brighter in one frame. This is most visible on → skip at low burn, where almost the whole plate is sooted.
issues.fix: Fade both terms with the finish: soot *= 1.0 - smoothstep(0.4, 1.0, uFinish); and the same factor on the EMBER_DEEP * glowHeat * 0.12 add.

issues.problem: cursor: none applies to the live plate before it is ready, and the custom cursor only shows with [data-ready]. During the load and the pre-sim, hovering the plate shows no cursor at all.
issues.fix: Change the selector to .scorch-plate[data-ready]:not(.scorch-plate--placeholder).

issues.problem: Audio is woken only on pointerdown. On Android Chrome a touch pointerdown does not count as user activation, so the first catch is silent and sound starts only from the second press.
issues.fix: Also call wakeSound() in handleUp, and fire catchFire's sound after a resume().then when the context was suspended.

issues.problem: HEAT_ALIVE is 0.08 but the ignition thresholdFloor is 0.07. The loop can stop while ink cells with heat between 0.07 and 0.08 are still able to catch, freezing a creeping front until the next interaction.
issues.fix: Set HEAT_ALIVE to 0.06, below SIM.thresholdFloor, or derive it as SIM.thresholdFloor * 0.85.

issues.problem: The loading fuse animates width through an @property, which forces a layout every frame. ClientOnly also swaps LoadingPlate for the stage's own plate, so the fuse animation restarts at 0 and the line jumps mid-load.
issues.fix: Draw the line with transform: scaleX(var(--scorch-fuse)) from transform-origin left and move the dot with translateX. Render one fuse element in ScorchExperience's .scorch-stage__plate, outside the swapped plate, and fade it on [data-status='ready'].

issues.problem: On a phone the touch-action: none plate is about 343 of 375px wide and roughly half the viewport tall. Vertical scrolling only works from the 16px gutters, the header or the caption, so reaching the panel below feels trapped.
issues.fix: At max-width 900px cap the plate at width: min(100%, 560px, 100svh - 320px) so the caption and the panel toggle stay in view, or add 24px side gutters around the plate on coarse pointers.

issues.problem: rect is refreshed only on pointerenter and pointerdown. After a wheel scroll while hovering, the custom cursor and the --hunger lookup are offset by the scroll distance until the pointer leaves and re-enters.
issues.fix: Refresh rect in a passive window scroll listener (and in the ResizeObserver callback), or compute it from event.offsetX/offsetY on the plate.

issues.problem: The error-state scrim hard-codes rgba(241,245,249), a cool slate that does not match the page surface token or the warm paper.
issues.fix: Build the eased multi-stop scrim from color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface) N%, transparent).

critique.wowGap: Make paper marginal and leave the ink for the visitor: raise SIM.thresholdBase to about 0.40. In the sim, bare paper at that level creeps and then dies unless fanned, while ink still runs at about 0.25 UV/s. Move the intro ignition to a low-fuel spot on the lower-left edge and stop it at about 12% burnt. The first frame is then a small glowing bite with a toast halo. The visitor's first hold on the black lettering sends a fuse racing about 8x faster than anything on screen, and the pale paper visibly stays standing as islands, which is the brief's exact wow.

build.summary: Loom shows one of Herb's recent album covers as woven cloth: 96 weft rows and 96 warp columns (64 on phones), drawn by a single raw WebGL2 fragment shader. The weave can be twill, plain or satin, and each float is a rounded capsule with one cylindrical shade and a faint ply twist that slides with the thread. Each thread's offset comes from a CPU spring chain with neighbour coupling, stepped at a fixed 1/480 s, and the offsets reach the GPU as a 128×4 R32F texture. Each thread samples the cover along its own path. A drag locks to an axis after 8px, holds the thread exactly under the pointer, bends the threads next to it, and lets go with the flick's velocity, and two fingers can hold two threads. Strips that slide past the edge show the previous or next cover, like a slot reel. Next and previous weave the new cover in row by row (rows slide in from the side, then warp columns pop in at 0→1.02→1), and each thread plays a Karplus–Strong pentatonic pluck when it crosses home (warp a fifth lower and panned). There is a visible mute button, a panel with presets (Silk, Linen, Canvas), weave, threads, tension, coupling and damping, rolling SlotNumber readouts, and keyboard control (←/→ change cover, ↑/↓ pick a row, Shift+←/→ pull it, Space plucks it).
build.wowMoment: Grab one row in the middle and throw it sideways. The rows around it bend with it, a shear ripple runs up and down the cloth with strips of the next cover showing at the edges, and as the threads spring home they play a quick falling pentatonic strum. Pressing → makes the next record weave in: a wave runs top to bottom as the rows slide in, the album plays a falling arpeggio, and then the warp threads pop back in across the cloth.
build.knownIssues: Never run in a browser, as instructed. All three checks pass: lab-gate, compile-check and glsl-check. I checked the look by porting the shader line for line to a CPU renderer and rendering real fallback cover cards to PNG (twill and satin, mid-strum and pulled). I checked the engine by running it headless against a mocked WebGL2 context and AudioContext: the intro, drag and release, a cover change, a tap, a key pull and a thread-count change all ran, the loop went idle when the cloth settled, and destroy ran cleanly. Pluck timing was counted in the same run. The real GPU compile is untested, though the GLSL ES 3.00 avoids reserved words and pow on negative bases, and a compile failure falls back to the flat cover with a note. Deliberate departures from the brief: (1) Raw WebGL2 in one engine module instead of R3F. (2) Default Linen springs (tension 160, coupling 2400, damping 7) plus a velocity-difference term between neighbouring threads, chosen so a shear wave actually travels; the brief's values (220, 900, 16) are close to the Canvas preset, and cover changes add landing damping (ζ about 0.66) so the new cover does not overshoot about 40%. (3) A thread plucks when it crosses home, once per swing, with the same note blocked for 120ms, at most 8 voices and master gain −18dB; a hard release still sounds about 10 notes as a strum, which might be busier than Herb wants. (4) The ←/→ keys work anywhere on the page, and ↑/↓/Shift/Space only when the canvas has focus. (5) Warp threads vanish instantly at the start of a cover or weave change and then pop back in; the image colours stay continuous because the wefts underneath carry the old cover. (6) Neighbour covers that are still loading show as a neutral grey strip until they arrive. The intro strum plays silently, because audio can only start after the first gesture.

critique.firstFrame:
In dev, which is the only place Herb judges it (lab pieces 404 in prod), the page is broken. The chrome rises in and the striped grey placeholder shows. Then the stage fails and you get a flat, static cover with the note "This loom needs WebGL2, so the cover sits flat."

The cause is React StrictMode (on by default in the App Router). It mounts, destroys and remounts the engine on the same React-owned canvas. destroy() calls loseContext(), so the second getContext('webgl2') returns that dead context. createShader returns null, compile throws, and onError('shader') fires.

With that fixed, the first frame is good. A woven cover blurs in at scale 0.965 while rows 20–70 hold an S-curve. They release top-down with a 9ms stagger and land with an overshoot. It is silent until the first touch. The 240ms hold is mostly hidden under the 520ms blur, so the strum is seen soft.
critique.checks:
1. node scripts/lab-gate.mjs loom: PASS.
2. compile-check loom: PASS (8 modules).
3. glsl-check src/app/lab/loom: ok for both shaders (loomShader.js:1 vertex, loomShader.js:8 fragment). There are no interpolations, so the check is meaningful.

All three pass, but the blocker is invisible to them because it only appears at runtime.

issues.problem: The engine is created on the React-owned <canvas>, and destroy() calls WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext() (loomEngine.js:935). StrictMode's mount, cleanup, remount cycle hands the second createLoom the same lost context. createProgram and createShader return null, compile throws, onError('shader') fires, and the page shows the flat 'needs WebGL2' fallback on every dev load. The same happens in prod whenever the effect re-runs, for example when prefers-reduced-motion is toggled.
issues.fix: Follow MarbleScene.jsx. Render a wrapper <div> and, inside the effect, document.createElement('canvas') with className loom-canvas, tabIndex 0 and the aria-label. Append it, pass it to createLoom, and on cleanup run engine.destroy() then canvas.remove(). As a backstop, at the top of createLoom treat gl.isContextLost() as 'retry on a fresh canvas', not 'shader'.

issues.problem: On a cover change, warp.popStart is set in the future and popCurve(t<0) returns 0, so every warp thread drops to zero thickness on frame 0. In twill that is half the cloth: it blinks to dark ground and 0.8-shaded weft for 280–700ms before the warps pop in from 0, not the brief's 0.84→1.02→1. That instant swap lands right under the wow moment. setParams has the same problem on a weave change (line 909).
issues.fix: Add a fifth state row, a per-warp reel index (0 = old cover, 1 = new), and sample uPrev or uCurrent in warpColour based on it. Keep each warp at full thickness on the old cover until its stagger time. At that moment flip its reel and run thickness through mix(0.84, 1.0, popCurve(t)), so it pops 0.84→1.02→1 and never disappears. For a weave change, pop from 0.84 as well, never from 0.

issues.problem: ensureAudio() only runs on pointerdown and keydown. Under the HTML user-activation rules, a touch pointerdown is not activation-triggering (only mouse pointerdown and non-mouse pointerup are). On phones the AudioContext is born suspended and resume() is rejected, so the first fling is silent, and on iOS sound may never start. Sound is half of this piece's pitch.
issues.fix: Also call ensureAudio() in onPointerUp before finishPointer, and in the mute toggle and prev/next click handlers (expose engine.primeAudio()). In pluck, if context.state is 'suspended', call resume() and drop that one note rather than queueing it.

issues.problem: The proximity indicator Herb asked for will be invisible. The threads already fill 84% of the cell (radius 0.42), so the 1.06 hover and 1.12 grab swell adds about 0.25–0.5 CSS px to a roughly 7.7px thread, and min(…, 0.49) clamps it further.
issues.fix: Open the rest gap: GAP 0.12, so the radius at rest is 0.38. Raise hover to 1.14 and grab to 1.26 (SWELL_PEAK 0.26) so the clamp still holds. Also brighten swollen threads: colour *= 1.0 + 0.5*(thick-1.0), which gives about +7% at a full grab. The bell then reads as a lens moving over the cloth.

issues.problem: In the default Twill, a pulled weft row only shows its slid strip on its own floats, half the crossings. The other half are warp floats that never moved, so a flung row reads as dashed, checkered noise rather than the clean slot-reel strips the wow moment promises. Column pulls have the same problem in reverse.
issues.fix: Let a displaced thread lift over the weave. Compute float lift = smoothstep(0.004, 0.03, abs(weftOffset) - abs(warpOffset)), and treat weft as on top when weftOver(row, col) or lift > 0.5; do the same for warp. Crossfade top and under with lift so the switch is smooth. Moving threads then ride on top as continuous strips and sink back into the twill as they settle.

issues.problem: Each next or prev press does weft.x[i] += direction with no clamp. Mashing → stacks offsets up to 4–5 widths, so rows whip across several widths at about 60 widths/s. The shader maps every reel below -0.5 to uPrev and every reel above 0.5 to uNext, so the same cover repeats along the strip. A multi-step jump also makes reel -1 show target-1 rather than the cover that was on screen, an instant swap.
issues.fix: Before adding, clamp: weft.x[i] = Math.max(-0.35, Math.min(0.35, weft.x[i])) + direction, and do the same for pinned targets and grab.base. When ringDistance(target, current) > 1, show the old cover with a one-off uPrev/uNext override, or step through one cover at a time.

issues.problem: Karplus–Strong buffers are synthesised lazily inside stepChain substeps, at roughly 170k float ops each. The first cover-change arpeggio builds up to 16 of them in quick succession, which causes a frame hitch exactly when the cloth is sweeping.
issues.fix: In createPluckBank, precompute all 16 weft and 16 warp buffers right after creation, in requestIdleCallback chunks of 4 (setTimeout fallback), as the brief specified. bufferFor then only reads from the Map.

issues.problem: uSuper switches on when the device-pixel cell size drops below 9. Once the governor lowers scale (for example a phone at 9.7px stepping to about 7.8px), 4× supersampling turns on and fragment cost rises about 2.5× instead of falling. The governor's trial reverts, so on struggling devices it can never shed load.
issues.fix: Decide supersampling from the cell size at the un-governed DPR (clothPx / governor.scale / threads), or drop to 2 taps when governor.scale < 1.

issues.problem: for (const grab of grabs.values()) sits inside the per-thread loop, which allocates about 256 Map iterators per running frame.
issues.fix: Once per frame, copy grab axis/index pairs into a preallocated Int16Array (up to 10 pointers) and loop over that.

issues.problem: heldUntil is stamped when the texture loads. If the tab is hidden or the canvas offscreen at load, the stamps expire and every row releases at once, so there is no stagger. The 240ms hold also sits under the 520ms blur reveal, so the S-curve is seen out of focus.
issues.fix: Set introPending and start the intro on the first active frame after the cover is ready. Set INTRO_HOLD_MS to about 420 so the release begins once the blur has mostly cleared.

issues.problem: On phones the tune panel opens below the caption. On a 667px-tall screen it lands below the fold, so tapping the button shows no visible response.
issues.fix: On open, requestAnimationFrame then panel.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' }), or present it as a bottom sheet.

issues.problem: A real context loss (GPU reset, backgrounded phone) sends the page to the permanent flat fallback, labelled 'needs WebGL2', which is wrong. There is no restore path.
issues.fix: preventDefault on lost (already done), then listen for webglcontextrestored and rebuild program, VAO and textures. Word the note by kind, not as 'needs WebGL2'.

issues.problem: The fallback captions read 'Card 01' / 'Local scans', which looks like placeholder slop whenever Spotify is down.
issues.fix: Use the real card names and makers from public/flyout/CREDITS.md.

issues.problem: GROUND_SHADE 0.44 lays a dark screen-door mesh across the whole cover, which darkens the art and leans toward depth-shading on a light page.
issues.fix: Use a ground of mix(under, vec3(0.93, 0.94, 0.95), 0.35) * 0.78 so the gaps read as light warp-room rather than shadow.

critique.wowGap:
Make a pulled thread lift over the weave. In shadeAt, compute lift = smoothstep(0.004, 0.03, abs(weftOffset) - abs(warpOffset)), and the mirror value for warp. Any thread that is displaced more than the one crossing it is drawn on top across every crossing, crossfaded by lift.

A flung row, plus the rows coupled to it, then becomes continuous strips of the picture sliding like slot reels across the whole width, instead of half-hidden dashes under stationary warp floats. As the springs bring them home, they sink back into the twill one by one in time with their plucks. That is the brief's zig-zag-into-strips moment made legible.

This change only lands once the StrictMode/loseContext blocker is fixed, because until then the loom never renders in dev.

changes: LoomStage.jsx: the stage now renders a host div and creates a fresh canvas with document.createElement inside the effect, carrying className loom-canvas, tabIndex 0 and the aria-label. Cleanup runs engine.destroy() and then canvas.remove(), so StrictMode's remount always gets a live context. If createLoom returns LOST_CONTEXT, the stage retries once on a new canvas. It also hands the engine up through onEngine.
loomEngine.js: createLoom returns LOST_CONTEXT when gl.isContextLost() is true, as the backstop. Program, VAO, quad and textures are now built in buildGpu() so they can be rebuilt.

loomEngine.js: real context loss now has a restore path. On loss the engine stops the loop and drops the textures. On webglcontextrestored it rebuilds the GPU objects and re-uploads every cover from the 512px source canvas it keeps for each. It reports 'lost' only if no restore arrives within 2.5s.

loomEngine.js: added a fifth state row holding a reel index per warp. On a cover change each warp stays at full thickness on the old cover. At its stagger time it switches to the new cover and pops 0.84 → 1.02 → 1, using POP_BACK 1.9 and mix(0.84, 1, popCurve). Weave and thread-count changes pop from 0.84 the same way and never drop to 0.

loomEngine.js + loomShader.js: the shader now has five cover samplers (current-2 to current+2), so a row offset by two covers shows the real cover. Before each press, row offsets, pinned targets and grab.base are clamped to ±(2 - steps). A jump of two covers after a pending load is handled as a 2-step reel, and warp reels shift with it. Mashing next or prev therefore no longer stacks widths or repeats covers.

loomEngine.js: the intro starts on the first active frame after the cover is ready, and onPainted fires only after that. INTRO_HOLD_MS is now 420, so the S-curve releases once the blur has mostly cleared. A hidden tab or offscreen canvas no longer collapses the stagger.

loomEngine.js: audio is primed on pointerup as well as pointerdown, and engine.primeAudio(force) is exposed. The prev/next chips, ←/→ keys and the mute toggle call it. The mute toggle forces it, so unmuting unlocks audio.

loomEngine.js: supersampling is decided from the cell size at the un-governed DPR, and drops to 2 taps (a new shader path) once the governor has lowered the scale. Grabs are copied once per frame into preallocated Int8Array/Int16Array buffers, so the per-thread Map iteration is gone. SWELL_PEAK is now 0.26.

loomShader.js (the wow change): a thread that is displaced more than the one crossing it now rides on top at every crossing. The lift is smoothstep(0.004, 0.03, slip(mine) - slip(other)), with top and under crossfaded by it, and the float scans extend through lifted cells. A flung row and the rows coupled to it slide as continuous strips and sink back into the twill as their springs bring them home. slip() measures distance to the nearest whole offset, so rows waiting at one full cover width still look woven until they move. A uSlip uniform skips the extra texel fetches when the cloth is still.

loomShader.js: GAP is now 0.12 (rest radius 0.38) and hover swell 1.14. Swollen threads brighten by up to about 7% (swellGlow), so the proximity bell reads as a lens. The ground is now mix(under, (0.93, 0.94, 0.95), 0.35) * 0.78, which reads as light warp-room rather than shadow.

loomAudio.js: all 16 weft and 16 warp Karplus–Strong buffers are precomputed in requestIdleCallback chunks of 4 (setTimeout fallback), and the work is cancelled on close. If the context is suspended, pluck calls resume() and drops that note.

LoomExperience.jsx: the failure note is now worded by kind (webgl, shader or lost). For shader and lost there is a Rethread button that remounts the stage. On phones, opening the tune panel scrolls it into view (smooth, or instant under reduced motion). The engine reference is kept in a ref through the onEngine callback.
loom.css: added .loom-host sizing, the note as a flex column with an 8px gap, the .loom-retry pill, and scroll-margin-bottom on the mobile panel. All vertical values are multiples of 4.

page.js: the fallback covers now use the real card names and makers from public/flyout/CREDITS.md (Honus Wagner / T206 White Border, Babe Ruth / Goudey Gum Company 1933, and so on) instead of 'Card 01' / 'Local scans'.
experiment.json: already complete (title Loom, two-sentence description, 4 tags, intent, building false, status candidate); left unchanged.
Verification: lab-gate PASS, compile-check PASS (8 modules), glsl-check ok on both shaders. The fragment and vertex shaders also compile cleanly under glslc as a real-compiler cross-check.
polish.remaining: Not checked in a browser, as the hard rules require. Herb should judge at /lab/loom in dev, in particular: whether the lifted-strip crossfade and the 0.84 warp pop feel right, the brightness of the swollen-thread glow, and how the lighter ground reads on very dark covers. Reduced motion still swaps covers instantly, which is intended. A third rapid next press can still swap a still-held row straight to the next cover, by design of the ±2 reel reach. DPR is still capped at 2 on the page, adaptive through the governor; it was not lowered to 1.5.

build.summary: Stir sets Herb's recent tracks (or the Please Please Me tracklist as a fallback) as a full-bleed wall of Geist Mono. Each row is justified edge to edge, and on a phone each row becomes one track spread across the width. Weight is the dye in a CPU stable-fluids simulation that runs on the same character grid. The simulation has anisotropic cells, semi-Lagrangian advection, 14 warm-started Jacobi pressure passes, vorticity confinement at ε 0.18, and dye that relaxes with e^(−dt/2.4s). It costs about 0.8ms per frame at 164×37 cells, measured in node. One WebGL2 pass draws it: a glyph atlas holds every character at 17 weight masters (100 to 900), and each pixel mixes the two nearest masters using bilinear dye, so weight changes smoothly even across a single letter and nothing reflows. Hovering stirs gently up to about 700, and pressing and dragging stirs hard up to 900. Holding still while pressed lets a blot well up, a tap drops an expanding bold ring, two fingers give two stirrers, the arrow keys send a current in from that side, and R calms the wall over 600ms. A "wght" readout rolls with SlotNumber, and its own font weight follows the peak weight in the wall. The loop sleeps when the fluid settles and pauses when the tab is hidden or the wall is offscreen. Every GL object is deleted and the context is released on unmount.
build.wowMoment: On load the type sweeps in from left to right, going from hairline weight 100 up to 430. A gust then blows in from the left at mid-height, and its bold head rolls into two counter-rotating lobes that keep curling after the gust has stopped. If you whip a loop through the wall, the bold vortex keeps spinning on its own, with song titles swelling and thinning as it curls, then it fades back into a quiet tracklist. The wght readout rolls up to 900 and grows bolder itself.
build.knownIssues: I have not looked at it in a browser, as the rules required. The fluid and the wall layout were run in node: the sim stays stable with no NaN, the intro gust rolls up into a vortex pair, and it settles in about 8s. The shader passed the GLSL parse check, but nothing has compiled it on a GPU yet. Things to check by eye: where the glyphs sit vertically in their cells (the baseline comes from the cap and x heights), and whether Safari's canvas honours numeric weights that aren't multiples of 100 (if it doesn't, the code falls back to 9 masters automatically). I did not use resolutionGovernor. The GPU pass is one cheap fragment shader, and dropping the DPR would reflow the character grid, so instead the frame adapts by cutting Jacobi passes from 14 to 8 when the sim takes more than 4ms. With only a few real tracks, rows can repeat exactly and form columns. Non-Latin titles are dropped from the wall, though they stay in the screen-reader list. In the hidden 4×4 preload iframe, the intro still plays once and the loop idles after about 8s. A click's ring is drawn by the shader and is not pushed into the fluid. A divergent push would have been removed by the pressure step anyway, so the click leaves only a bold dot in the fluid.

critique.firstFrame: The server render shows the header ("Stir", the hint, and a "wght 430" gauge on the right) fading up with a 4px blur over 600ms, above an empty paper-coloured stage. Fonts are preloaded, so after one effect tick WebGL2 starts. The canvas switches to opacity 1 on its first frame, but every cell is still paper, so the switch can't be seen. The wall then sweeps in from left to right over about 1.4s: letters come in at weight 100 with alpha and settle to 430, with per-cell jitter. At 0.45s a scripted gust at about 2000 px/s enters from the left edge at mid-height, while the left columns are still settling. Because it lays dye at cap 1 along its whole path, it reads first as a horizontal bold-900 stripe across the left 42% of the wall. Only the decelerating head rolls into a mushroom dipole. The gauge rolls up toward 900 and back down, and everything relaxes over about 7s. The wall itself is strong and legible: a full-bleed Geist Mono tracklist in calm 430 ink, with justified rows of "01 I Saw Her Standing There  The Beatles  2:55". The intro currently shows a bar more than the "two counter-rotating bold vortices" the brief calls for.
critique.checks:
All three checks pass, and no file was edited.
1. `node scripts/lab-gate.mjs stir` prints PASS (lint, comments, type system, tokens).
2. `compile-check.mjs stir` prints PASS (9 modules).
3. `glsl-check.mjs src/app/lab/stir` reports ok for both shaders in `stirShader.js` (lines 1 and 8). They are plain strings with no interpolation, so the undeclared-identifier check is meaningful.

I also checked the APIs by hand, and all are valid:
- R16F with RED/FLOAT data upload, LINEAR filtering on R16F, an R8 text texture read with `texelFetch`, and `UNPACK_ALIGNMENT` set to 1.
- A full-screen triangle from `gl_VertexID` with an empty VAO.
- Setting the `uRings[4]` array through its base location with `uniform4fv`.
- Texture orientation is consistent across the atlas, text and dye textures (no flip, y top-down everywhere).
- The Jacobi and gradient maths is correct for non-square cells, and the vorticity sign is correct in y-down coordinates.
- `SlotNumber.setValue` exists via `useImperativeHandle`, `--font-geist-mono` is inherited from `<html>`, and `getRecentTracks` provides `durationMs`.

SSR is safe because every window access happens inside the effect. Under strict-mode double mount, the first instance is destroyed before its `fonts.load` await resolves, so the second mount gets a fresh context.

issues.problem: The click or tap ring is visual only. dropRing adds a dye blob plus a shader-side weight band (uRings), but injects no velocity, so the 'radial impulse ring' never moves the ink. Tapping inside a spinning wake leaves the vortex untouched while a bold band passes over it like an overlay. That is a proximity effect, not fluid physics.
issues.fix: In dropRing, also splat an outward radial velocity. Loop over cells within the ring reach and add (dx,dy)/|d| * RING_IMPULSE * exp(-d²/r²), with RING_IMPULSE around 900 px/s and r = layout.radius*1.2. Add a fluid.impulse(x,y,strength,radius) helper in stirFluid.js so it stays allocation-free. Keep the shader ring as the visible crest so existing bold ink is pushed out in step with it.

issues.problem: The intro gust stamps with pressed=true along its whole path, so dye reaches cap 1 from x=-26 to 42% of the width. The first frame reads as a thick horizontal bold bar with a curled tip, not the brief's two counter-rotating vortices. This is the one scripted moment, and it undersells the mechanic.
issues.fix: Give gusts their own dye profile: no dye for the first 55% of GUST_LIFE, then dye at 0.7 only at the head. Use force only on the leading third. Alternatively, replace the intro with a ghost stirrer that draws one tight 0.7s loop (see wowGap). The velocity jet then forms the dipole on its own, and only the mushroom head carries ink.

issues.problem: Release drops the last segment of a flick. On touch, the stirrer is deleted in release() before the next frame stamps its pending x/y, so the fastest part of a flick (the last 8-16ms) is never injected. On mouse, pressed is set false first, so that segment is stamped at hover force 0.45 instead of 0.9. Flicks end weakly, which works against 'a flick off the edge leaves a wake that keeps going'.
issues.fix: In release(), if stirrer.x/y differs from lastX/lastY, call stamp(lastX,lastY,x,y,vx,vy,true,1/60,P.FORCE) before clearing pressed. Alternatively, set stirrer.releasing = true and delete it in driveStirrers after its final stamp.

issues.problem: Neither lostpointercapture nor window blur is handled. If a pointerup is missed (alt-tab mid-drag, OS gesture, devtools), the stirrer stays pressed=true. The WELL branch then keeps injecting dye every frame, the wall never settles, and the loop never sleeps.
issues.fix: Listen for 'lostpointercapture' on the stage, calling release(event, true), and for window 'blur', clearing pressed on every stirrer and deleting non-mouse ones. Remove both listeners in detach().

issues.problem: Weight 430 at rest sits between the 400 and 450 masters, so every glyph at rest is a 60/40 crossfade of two rasters. That is slightly soft and double-edged, and it shows in the state seen most.
issues.fix: Build the masters so REST_WEIGHT lands exactly on one. For example, anchor the ladder at 430 with step 47 (430, 477 … 900) plus a few below for the entrance. Pass masterBase to the shader as a uniform and use master = (weight - uMasterBase) / uMasterStep.

issues.problem: Plain mouse hover deposits dye up to cap 0.55, which is weight about 700. Just moving the cursor across the wall to read leaves heavy trails, so hover and drag feel close together and press-drag loses its 'strong stir' contrast.
issues.fix: Lower HOVER_DYE_CAP to about 0.3 (weight about 560) and HOVER_FORCE to about 0.35. Hover then reads as a gentle stir, and pressing clearly pours ink.

issues.problem: Press feedback is slow. A stationary press only wells dye at 1.4/s, so nothing visible happens for about 150ms. The tap ring only fires on pointerup. stage.dataset.pressed is set but no CSS uses it, and the stage has no cursor affordance.
issues.fix: On pointerdown, splat an immediate small dye bloom (0.4, radius*0.5) so the touch point goes bold on the first frame. In stir.css, add `.stir__stage { cursor: crosshair; -webkit-touch-callout: none; }` and use [data-pressed] for the grabbing state, or remove the dead attribute.

issues.problem: The loader was copied from a covers experiment. It names things covers and FALLBACK_COVERS with /flyout images, drops tracks without art, dedupes by album image (so several songs from one album collapse to one), and throws when fewer than 6 remain. The result is a needlessly thin tracklist or an early fall-back to the Beatles.
issues.fix: Map tracks to {title, artist, durationMs}, dedupe by id or by title+artist, drop the image requirement, require at least 3, and rename everything to tracks. tracksFrom already handles the fallback.

issues.problem: destroy() calls loseContext on the canvas. When Fast Refresh re-runs the effect on the same canvas element, getContext('webgl2') returns the lost context. setupGpu then throws, so the dev route drops to the StillWall fallback until a full reload.
issues.fix: Key the canvas in StirStage on a counter that increments per effect run, so each mount gets a fresh element. Alternatively, skip loseContext and only delete the GL objects.

issues.problem: Cell width is rounded to whole device pixels, which quantises the tracking law away. At 13px with DPR 1 the cell is 8px, not 7.757, so the type sits 0.24px per character looser than the law, and the error changes with DPR.
issues.fix: Choose fontCss per breakpoint so that fontCss*0.6 - 0.043*(fontCss-12) multiplied by DPR is close to an integer. Alternatively, keep the fractional cell and sample the atlas with LINEAR filtering using an offset tile origin.

issues.problem: texture() is called inside non-uniform control flow (if code > 0.5). Implicit derivatives are technically undefined there. It is harmless without mipmaps, but some drivers warn.
issues.fix: Use textureLod(uDye, ..., 0.0) and textureLod(uAtlas, ..., 0.0) inside the branch.

issues.problem: A DPR change (moving the window to another display) is not watched. The canvas stays at the old resolution until a size change happens.
issues.fix: Add a matchMedia(`(resolution: ${devicePixelRatio}dppx)`) change listener that calls scheduleResize and re-arms itself, and remove it in detach().

critique.wowGap: The brief's wow moment is a tight loop whose bold vortex keeps spinning after the hand leaves, and that is the one thing the page never shows unprompted. Replace the intro gust with a ghost stirrer: a pressed virtual pointer entering the stirrers map at INTRO_GUST_AT. It draws one quick clockwise loop of about 0.7s and about 90px radius, slightly off-centre, with an eased-in/eased-out angular speed. Then it lifts and leaves. Inject dye only during the loop and no ring. The first frame then shows the core claim: a bold whorl of song titles swelling to 900 keeps turning by itself for about 2s after the "hand" has gone, then dies back to quiet 430 type. Pair this with the radial velocity impulse on tap, so a visitor's first tap visibly blows that whorl apart.

changes: stirWall.js: the scripted gust intro is gone. At 0.5s a 'ghost' stirrer is added to the stirrers map. It is pressed and uses the same stirring code as a real pointer. It draws one clockwise loop of about 1.1 turns in 0.72s, with eased-in/eased-out angular speed. The loop is slightly off-centre at 42%/54% of the wall and has a radius of 72-110px. The path spirals inward, and dye rises from 0.3 at the tail to full strength at the head. The result is a comma-shaped whorl that keeps turning after the ghost lifts. It injects no ring and is skipped under reduced motion.

stirFluid.js: added an allocation-free impulse(x, y, strength, width, front, reach). It adds outward radial velocity into preallocated kick arrays. step() applies the kicks after projection and before dye advection. A radial push has no curl, so the pressure projection would erase it before it moved any ink; adding it after projection avoids that.

stirWall.js: while a tap ring is active, driveRings pushes velocity at the ring's crest every frame (0.8 × crest speed, starting around 900 px/s, band = radius × 0.9). Ink and momentum now ride outward with the visible ring, so a tap breaks up an existing whorl. RING_STRENGTH is lowered to 0.65 so the moving ink carries the effect more than the shader band.

stirWall.js: stamp() now takes brush objects (hover, press, ghost, gust) that are allocated once. Arrow-key gusts lay no dye for the first 55% of their life, then ramp to 0.7 dye at the head only, so the jet forms a mushroom instead of a stripe.

stirWall.js: release() takes the pointerup position and stamps the last segment of the flick with the press brush before clearing `pressed` or deleting the stirrer. A new stirStep() helper is shared with driveStirrers.
stirWall.js: added 'lostpointercapture' (releases if still pressed) and window 'blur' (unpresses every real stirrer and deletes the non-mouse ones). Both are removed in detach().
stirWall.js: pointerdown immediately drops a small dye bloom (cap 0.45, radius × 0.5). stir.css: added cursor: crosshair, -webkit-touch-callout: none, and cursor: grabbing on [data-pressed].
stirParams.js: HOVER_DYE_CAP is now 0.3 (weight about 530) and HOVER_FORCE is 0.35. Added the ghost, gust-dye, ring-carry, bloom, font-size and master-ladder constants.

stirAtlas.js and stirShader.js: the weight masters now step outward from 430 in steps of 47 (101 to 900, 18 masters), so rest weight sits exactly on a master. The coarse fallback uses steps of 94. A new uMasterBase uniform drives master = (weight - uMasterBase) / uMasterStep.

stirWall.js measure(): the cell width is rounded to whole device pixels first, then the font size is solved back from the tracking formula: font = (cell + 0.043 × 12) / (advance - 0.043). The tracking law now holds exactly at every DPR; 13px becomes 13.44px with an 8px cell.
stirShader.js: texture() inside the branch is replaced with textureLod(..., 0.0) for both the atlas and the dye.
stirWall.js: a matchMedia resolution listener re-arms itself and calls scheduleResize when the DPR changes. It is removed in detach().

stirWall.js and StirStage.jsx: the wall now creates its own canvas and removes it in destroy(). Every effect run gets a fresh element, so loseContext no longer breaks Fast Refresh. canvasRef is removed from StirStage.

page.js: the loader is renamed to loadTracks and maps tracks to {title, artist, durationMs}. It dedupes by id or title|artist, no longer requires artwork, needs at least 3 tracks, and keeps up to 40. It passes recent={tracks} and falls back to [] so tracksFrom uses the Beatles. The isProdView guard is kept.
stirTracks.js: tracksFrom(recent) no longer has the placeholder-artist cover filter.
StirExperience.jsx and StirStage.jsx: the hint reads 'Whip a loop through the tracklist, tap to scatter it.' The key line is shortened, and the aria-label now describes the outward ring.
experiment.json: rewrote the two-sentence description and the intent, set tags to Type/Simulation/WebGL/Music, title Stir, building false, status still candidate.
polish.remaining: All three checks pass: lab-gate PASS, compile-check PASS (9 modules), and glsl-check ok for both shaders. Not run in a browser (as instructed), so these values are set by reasoning and not yet seen on screen: the ghost loop's speed and size (GHOST_SECONDS 0.72, GHOST_TURN 1.12 turns, GHOST_SHARE/MIN/MAX), the ring push strength (RING_CARRY 0.8, RING_BAND_SIZE 0.9) and the gust dye timing. One known side effect: the radial push is not fully removed by the 14-iteration pressure solve, so a little outward flow lasts a few frames after a ring ends. It is bounded by MAX_SPEED and the velocity decay. A resize that changes the grid during the first second cancels the ghost intro.

build.summary: Thread is a real Up Next queue of Herb's ten most recent tracks on a flat white card. One elastic thread runs through every round cover, so each cover sits on it like a bead. The thread is a 1D wave-equation string (c = 1100px/s, γ = 3.6/s, 4 nodes per row, substepped at up to 240Hz and pinned at both ends). It is drawn as a single 2px round-capped Catmull-Rom path on Canvas2D, with a small knot at each end. It thins slightly as it stretches. Every cover rides the thread exactly. Row text sways by 0.6·u, capped at 14px. Rows move on springs (380/24), the card's sheet shrinks and grows on a tail spring, and the song count, minutes and row numbers roll through SlotNumber. One rAF loop, driven by refs, writes transforms only for values that changed. It sleeps when the energy drops below 0.01, when the tab is hidden and when the card is offscreen. React commits the order only when a gesture ends. Each removal, drop or undo plays a Karplus-Strong pluck (default on, with a small sound toggle in the header). Its pitch comes from the thread's current length, snapped to a pentatonic scale, so the note rises as the queue gets shorter.
build.wowMoment: Flick the third song off hard. The bead lets go and the thread snaps: the stretched elastic collapses in about 35ms and a wave runs down the seven rows below, each cover swaying sideways in turn while the gap closes with spring overshoot. The numbers roll, a plucked note rings, and an Undo toast pops in. Undo slides the song back in from the right, where it hooks onto the thread with a pluck of its own. When the queue is empty, Refill threads all ten back on at a 40ms stagger, and the plucks fall in pitch like a harp glissando as the thread lengthens.
build.knownIssues:
I checked this with the gate, an esbuild compile, eslint (no warnings) and a headless test of the string physics (stable; a pinned V-shape and a travelling pulse both behave correctly). Per the rules, I never ran it in a browser, so none of the motion has been seen on screen. Known issues:
- Sound is on by default. It only starts after a user gesture, and the first pluck may be silent while the AudioContext resumes.
- Each row's list item box sits at the top of the list, with only its inner layers moved by transforms (this keeps the thread layered between the reveal and the row). Tabbing into the list may therefore scroll the page to the top of the list rather than to the focused row. Arrow-key focus and taps scroll correctly.
- After a pluck the loop keeps running for up to about 5s until the energy threshold is reached, though the motion stops being visible after about 2s.
- In a short iframe (76vh at 1280 wide), all ten 56px rows plus the header run just past the fold, so the bottom row needs a small scroll. The fixed hint/toast pill can overlap the last row.
- Edge auto-scroll while reordering is a simple per-frame scrollBy.
- The flick and pull amplitudes (pull cap 24, flick bump up to 20, total cap 42) are tuned by reasoning, not by eye.

critique.firstFrame: Before hydration the server render shows only an empty light card with the heading "Up next" and the line "0 songs · 0 min". The rows are hidden by `.thread:not([data-phase])` and the canvas is blank. In dev, hydration can take a second or more, so that is a long time to look at an empty card. After mount, a bare straight thread with two anchor dots shows first. Then the rows blur and fade in over it with a 40ms stagger and drop 24px on underdamped springs, and the counts roll to 10 songs and the real total in minutes. At 300ms a 10px pulse runs down the string. That pulse takes about 0.5s to cross the whole list, so it reads as a quick shiver, not the brief's "thread pulls taut". During the fade each `li` has opacity below 1, which makes it its own stacking context, so the 2px ink thread paints over the cover beads. Each bead then pops in front of the thread when its fade ends. After that it is a clean flat card with real Spotify covers. It looks good at rest, and the first touch has real weight: the press scales to 0.985, the bead follows the finger 1:1 into a tented V, the whole list leans, release twangs with a Karplus-Strong pluck, and the gap closes with overshoot.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate thread: PASS. 2. compile-check thread: PASS (7 modules). 3. glsl-check src/app/lab/thread: no shaders found. It is Canvas2D plus DOM, so the check does not apply.

issues.problem: The `rows` list puts exiting rows after the live ones, and reorders change the order array. So React moves `li` nodes with insertBefore. React 19.3 here has no moveBefore, so the move detaches and reattaches the node. That restarts the `thread-pop` keyframe on `.thread-bead[data-state=loaded] .thread-bead__image`. In the wow moment, the flicked row's cover drops to opacity 0 and blur and pops back in while it flies off. On Undo, every row below the restored one gets moved, so about 7 covers blink. On drag-drop and Alt+Arrow reorder, the moved row's cover blinks too. Its SlotNumber index also snaps instead of rolling, because a moved node has no before-change style, and the focused li loses focus and has to be refocused manually.
issues.fix: Keep DOM order stable and let transforms carry position. Render `tracks.filter(t => order.includes(t.id) || exiting.includes(t.id))` in original track order, and pass each row's live index as a prop (aria-posinset already conveys order). Also replace the cover's keyframe `animation` with a `transition` on opacity, filter and transform keyed off `[data-state=loaded]`, so a DOM move can never replay it.

issues.problem: The intro fade puts opacity: 0 and filter: blur(6px) on `.thread-row`. While either is active, every li becomes a z-index-auto stacking context that paints below `.thread-canvas` (z-index 1). For about 0.4 to 0.9s the ink thread is drawn over every cover bead, and each bead jumps in front of the thread when its transition ends, exactly while the intro pulse is running.
issues.fix: Move the intro fade and blur off the li and onto children that already sit inside the body's z-index 2 context: `.thread:not([data-phase]) .thread-bead, .thread:not([data-phase]) .thread-row__main { opacity: 0; filter: blur(6px) }` with the same staggered transition. Or give `.thread-rows` an explicit `z-index: 2` and lower the canvas to z-index 1 under it, keeping the reveal under the thread by moving it to a sibling layer.

issues.problem: With c = 1100px/s and nodes 14px apart, the wave crosses seven rows (392px) in about 0.36s, roughly 2 frames per row. Most of the energy comes from releasing a whole-string V (the pin is capped at 24px), so the list swings almost as one standing mode instead of showing the brief's 'wave running down the seven rows below, each one swaying in turn'. The fly bump (`addBump`, halfWidth 42) splits evenly up and down.
issues.fix: Lower WAVE_SPEED to about 520px/s, which gives about 100ms per row. On a removal, inject a downward-travelling `addPulse(string, beadY + 20, flick, 26)` (the one-directional pulse already in threadPhysics) instead of the symmetric `addBump`. Also lower PULL_CAP to about 14, so the drag V stays modest and the release reads as one legible ripple running down.

issues.problem: The toast and the hint swap instantly. On a removal the hint unmounts with no exit and the toast pops in. After 5.2s the toast vanishes in one frame and the hint re-pops after a 600ms delay. Rapid removals re-mount the toast each time. It is the only instant cut on a page that otherwise has physical weight, and `aria-live` on the whole dock re-announces the hint every time.
issues.fix: Keep the last toast mounted with `data-state="leaving"`. Give it a 180ms ease-out exit (opacity plus scale 0.96 plus 4px blur), and unmount on animationend. Crossfade the hint in after that with no 600ms delay. Put `aria-live` on the toast element only.

issues.problem: The server render shows '0 songs · 0 min' with no rows and no thread, and stays that way until hydration plus two rAFs plus 160ms. The brief's first frame is 'Up next · 10 songs · 38 min' with the list settling. Rows also flash '00' before the index roll. On a slow dev hydrate the vote frame is an empty card.
issues.fix: Server-render the real values: pass `value={songs}` from the start and run the count-up only as a client enhancement after mount. Give each row an initial inline `transform: translate3d(0, rowTop(index)px, 0)` in ThreadRow so the noscript and pre-hydration layout is correct. Then hide only with opacity and let the intro drop from there.

issues.problem: The thread is drawn straight and taut the moment the component mounts, before any row is visible. Nothing makes it 'pull taut', so the thread itself has no entrance, only a 10px pulse at 300ms.
issues.fix: Start the string slack: seed u with a soft sine sag (for example 8px at mid) and pin nothing, so it springs taut as the rows drop. Alternatively reveal the canvas stroke top-to-bottom over 360ms on --ease-entrance and fire the pulse when the stroke reaches the first bead.

issues.problem: A release past 35% of the width removes the row even when the finger is flicking back to the left. The user's 'never mind' gesture deletes the song anyway.
issues.fix: Require `velocity > -0.15` for the distance-based removal: `(reach > width * REMOVE_FRACTION && velocity > -0.15) || (velocity > FLICK_SPEED && reach > 16)`.

issues.problem: A 220ms long-press on touch is shorter than iOS's roughly 500ms. A thumb that pauses mid-scroll to read lifts a row by accident.
issues.fix: Use 220ms for mouse and about 380ms when `event.pointerType === "touch"`. The handle keeps its instant lift.

issues.problem: REST_ENERGY 0.01 on Σu² + Σv², with v in px/s, keeps the sim and about 30 transform writes per frame going for roughly 5s after every pluck, long after motion has dropped under 0.05px. `writeSheet` also animates `height` on a shadowed element, which costs layout plus paint every frame while the tail springs.
issues.fix: Stop when max|u| < 0.05 and max|v| < 2, then snap to zero. Animate the sheet with `transform: scaleY` on a pseudo-element, or `clip-path: inset(0 0 Npx 0 round 16px)`, instead of `height`.

issues.problem: `listTop = list.offsetTop` is only refreshed by a ResizeObserver on the list. A font swap or header wrap that moves the list without resizing it leaves the sheet height a few px off the card. Each mouse pointermove also calls getBoundingClientRect right after the rAF transform writes.
issues.fix: Also observe `.thread-head` in the same ResizeObserver, and cache the list rect in `measure()` plus a passive scroll listener, so hover reads no layout.

issues.problem: The row title overrides text-ui-lg (14px, 440) with --font-weight-caption 520, which the ladder reserves for 11px captions. The bead `top: 10px` is off the 4px grid. Two raw colours, `rgb(15 23 42 / 0.08)` and `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.14)`, bypass the tokens.
issues.fix: Use the ladder's subsection weight token, or step the title to a token whose own weight carries the hierarchy. Centre the bead with `top: 50%; translate: 0 -50%`, or a 12px top with a 32px bead, and move the two colours to `--color-line-subtle` and an inverse-surface hover token.

issues.problem: When the Spotify fetch fails, the queue shows 'Card 01 by Local scans', which is not a song queue and goes against the brief's real-tracks requirement.
issues.fix: Use a small fallback list of real titles, artists and durations, paired with the local card images.

critique.wowGap: Slow the travelling wave down until it can be read. Drop WAVE_SPEED from 1100 to about 520px/s, and on a removal send a one-directional `addPulse` running down from the removed bead instead of the symmetric bump plus whole-string V release. Each of the rows below then visibly sways in turn, about 100ms apart, which is the exact wow moment in the brief. Right now it is lost as a half-second whole-list wobble.
